item.title: “That was unpleasant to see” Giancarlo Marocchi reacts to Juventus draw against Rennes
item.description: “That was unpleasant to see” Giancarlo Marocchi reacts to Juventus draw against Rennes Juventus were unable to secure another victory after facing Rennes in the Europa League last night, leaving the Bianconeri with several aspects of their game to improve as they look to return to winning ways. Juve produced a much stronger performance in the second half and came close to snatching victory in the closing minutes . They thought they had scored a decisive goal, but it was ruled out for offside following a review, forcing Juventus to settle for a draw. The Bianconeri have struggled to establish themselves among the leading clubs in Italy, with their domestic form remaining inconsistent. Despite their difficulties, their European performances have attracted attention, although they still need to turn their efforts into better results. Against Rennes, Juventus worked hard and showed determination, but they could not find the winning goal before the final whistle . Their improved performance after the interval offered some encouragement, yet their inability to maintain that level throughout the match remains a concern. Juventus must address their slow starts One of the recurring problems for Juventus in recent matches has been their tendency to improve only after half-time. Against Rennes, they allowed their opponents to dominate possession for a significant period, forcing Juve to spend too much time chasing the ball. Although Juventus eventually responded with greater intensity, their slow start made securing all three points more difficult. The team must learn to impose itself earlier in matches instead of relying on second-half improvements to rescue results. Former Juventus player Giancarlo Marocchi watched the match and assessed the team’s performance, identifying both positive aspects and areas that require attention. According to Tuttomercatoweb , he said: “If the reference is to the last match, then everything was fine. Overall, I saw a solid team, with everyone in their place. On the negative side, I saw a half-hour in which Rennes kept the ball and let the Juventus players run after them, and that was unpleasant to see. But then there was also a reaction.” (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) Juventus need greater consistency Marocchi’s assessment recognises the team’s response while highlighting the difficulties they experienced when Rennes controlled possession. Juventus showed they could react under pressure, but they need to demonstrate the same determination from the opening whistle. Improving their consistency and controlling matches more effectively will be essential if the Bianconeri want to return to winning ways. Their second-half display against Rennes offers some encouragement, but they must turn those positive spells into victories rather than allowing promising performances to end in disappointing draws.

item.title: Carrick ‘100%’ sure he can lead United forward; Dortmund take on the influencers: football – live
item.description: ⚽ All the latest news going into the weekend’s action ⚽ Premier League: weekend guide | Mail Tom Álvaro Arbeloa’s been talking ahead of Fulham’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, and buoyed up by last weekend’s much needed win over Hull. “Nothing has changed for us,” insisted the manager, “we were not winning games but we believed in ourselves, we were doing so many things well, “The most important thing [about the Hull win] is we were in same situation against Manchester United and Ipswich but didn’t win but now we had to improve in our transition and did. We controlled the ball in their half better than before.” As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Sunday’s match at Camp Nou will be watched by hundreds of millions of viewers all over the world. A clásico always carries significance, but this weekend’s edition will be especially significant. A Barça win would move them nine points clear of their rivals at the top of La Liga . A Real Madrid victory could be a catalyst for the rest of their season. Continue reading...

item.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Varun Chakravarthy? Exploring India's potential XI for 2nd T20I vs NZ at Christchurch
item.description: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Varun Chakravarthy? Exploring India's potential XI for 2nd T20I vs NZ at Christchurch originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: India ace Ishan Kishan is out of the second T20I with a low-grade adductor strain. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is a leading option, but Varun Chakravarthy could also come in. India lead the five-match series 1-0 ahead of Saturday’s second game at Hagley Oval. Will Varun Chakravarthy get the nod ahead of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi? Predicting India’s playing XI for 2nd T20I vs New Zealand India must now choose between a teenage batting prodigy and a proven spinner after an injury to Ishan Kishan opened up a spot in the side. The wicketkeeper-batter will miss the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday, and the team management is weighing its options after a record-breaking chase in the series opener. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has confirmed that Kishan suffered a low-grade right adductor strain during the first T20I. Its medical team is monitoring his progress, but he will not be available as India try to stretch their 1-0 lead in the five-match series. MORE: New Zealand vs India 2nd T20I prediction, lineups and Hagley Oval pitch report — who will win? His absence matters because he was part of the batting group that had been reshuffled for the opening game, where he was dismissed for one off three balls. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was in the squad but sat out the first match, and he is now one of the obvious candidates to replace Kishan. The 15-year-old has already made his senior international debut, and he was part of the gold-medal-winning men’s cricket team at the 2026 Asian Games. Picking him would therefore mean a return to the playing XI, which has been a talking point among fans for several matches. Speaking about Sooryavanshi, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said, “If Ishan doesn’t play, unless he recovers completely, which the medical team will advise, Vaibhav could definitely step in for him. He is one of the strongest contenders.” The decision is not as simple as swapping one batter for another. According to Revsportz , India could surprise people by going in a different direction and might prefer an extra bowling option in Varun Chakravarthy. If Sooryavanshi does come in, the order at the top becomes the next question. One is Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Sooryavanshi in that order, another is Abhishek, Sooryavanshi and Samson. MORE: Ishan Kishan injury: Sooryavanshi could play 2nd T20I vs New Zealand India predicted XI vs New Zealand for 2nd T20I at Christchurch This is a prediction built from the side that played the first T20I, with Sooryavanshi replacing Kishan. Chakravarthy would come in at the expense of one of the batters if the management chooses extra bowling. Abhishek Sharma Vaibhav Sooryavanshi Sanju Samson (wk) Shreyas Iyer (c) Tilak Varma Naman Dhir Axar Patel Nitis

Fans have wanted this for a while, and there is little downside in trying him in a series that India already lead. However, Chakravarthy's case deserves a hearing. India’s bowling attack is a lighter unit than usual, and a spinner like Chakravarthy could be a handy option. The best answer may depend on the pitch, which should be assessed on match day. Ideally, India would play Sooryavanshi and keep their bowling resources intact by resting a batter lower down the order, since Dhir and Reddy both bring some depth. Whatever the final call, the management should avoid treating the teenager as a stopgap. If he plays, he should get a clear role and a run of games, so the selection reads as a plan and not a reaction to an injury. item.title: Payton Westcott Grew Up Racing. Now the Promising Teenage Driver Is Proving She Belongs In F1 (Exclusive)
item.description: Payton Westcott Credit: Pauline Ballet - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty NEED TO KNOW Payton Westcott began competing in go-kart races at 11 after first driving a kart at age 6 The 17-year-old moved to Italy at 15 to pursue a career in open-wheel racing Westcott earned her first F1 Academy victory in August and is targeting a top-five debut season finish Payton Westcott has always been comfortable behind the wheel. The F1 Academy driver grew up in a racing-obsessed household and first gripped a steering wheel on her own when she was just 6 years old, after her dad, Kevin, put her in a go-kart as a form of “babysitting.” “It was really a thing at the track we went to growing up where all the men would put their kids in karting while they would go and drive on the track themselves, and it would distract the kids for a little while,” Westcott, 17, tells PEOPLE. “I drove for quite a while before one day my dad’s coach noticed me and said I wasn’t half bad, so he decided that he should try to put me into go-kart racing.” Westcott’s family “had no idea” about the world of go-kart racing until her father’s coach suggested she join — a recommendation that turned out to be a great one. Westcott continued to fall in love with racing and started competing in go-karting events at age 11. Four years later, at age 15, she moved to Italy full time to pursue racing open-wheeled cars as a career. “I’m eternally grateful to him for putting me in racing,” Westcott told F1 about her dad this past June. Now, the Laguna Beach, Calif., native continues to master courses around the world as one of the 15 full-time drivers in the all-female F1 Academy racing series, which comes to Austin, Texas, for its penultimate event of the season this weekend. And while she does get time away from the track, Westcott tells PEOPLE driving remains top of mind as she races in a simulation at home — “whether it’s going to a professional sim or just at home with my friends or playing and messing around.” Payton Westcott Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty An avid reader and casual television watcher, Westcott says she finds comfort in her books and cozy nights in with her family — when she has the chance to visit them back in California. But those visits have been so far between this year that her mother has lapped her in television shows they watch together. “She likes to skip ahead of me,” Westcott laughs. But there’s not much time for television when there are races to be won. Westcott has continued climbing the ranks of the sport she now loves just as much as her father. Fresh off her first-ever F1 Academy win this past August, Westcott is eyeing a top-5 finish in her debut season with the racing series, designed to recruit more women into the sport’s top racing series that has only seen five women enter an F1 Grand Prix weekend. And while she does get time away from the track, Westcott tells PEOPLE driving remains top of mind as she races in a simulation at home — “whether it’s going to a professional sim or just at home with my friends or playing and messing around.” Payton Westcott Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty An avid reader and casual television watcher, Westcott says she finds comfort in her books and cozy nights in with her family — when she has the chance to visit them back in California. But those visits have been so far between this year that her mother has lapped her in television shows they watch together. “She likes to skip ahead of me,” Westcott laughs. Fresh off her first-ever F1 Academy win this past August, Westcott is eyeing a top-5 finish in her debut season with the racing series, designed to recruit more women into the sport’s top racing series that has only seen five women enter an F1 Grand Prix weekend. Westcott told the F1 Academy website that it was an “incredible” feeling to get her first professional win in the series. “It takes a big weight off my shoulders,” the teenage up-and-comer said. “I really did it to prove to myself that I could do it, and I’m so happy.” Even as Westcott’s own career blossoms, she’s found inspiration from her rivals on the track. Payton Westcott Credit: Anni Graf - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty “I definitely look a lot to the others around me,” Westcott says. “I acknowledge and really pay close attention to everyone. Doriane [Pin, the F1 Academy 2025 Champion] is especially a great person to learn from.” Westcott says Pin has been coaching her this season and “it’s been really helpful to have her there,” pointing out the minute details she could focus on to improve her racing as her career rises. “It’s really helpful to have her there giving me advice and just helping me,” Westcott says. “And she’s such an incredible teammate and woman. I just feel so grateful that I get to learn from her and really grow with her.” The American F1 Academy star tells PEOPLE her focus now is to “end the year on a high note.” “I’m always looking to keep improving,” Westcott says, looking ahead to the series’ final two events in Texas and Nevada, and then to the 2027 season. “I think in racing, the best thing is just building your career as well as building your experience and building your level. So I want to keep improving, keep moving up.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Conte 'not in advanced negotiations' with any club amid Man Utd links
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Then Napoli manager Antonio Conte gestures on the touchline during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Napoli and Chelsea at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. (is associated with: «Conte 'not in advanced negotiations' with any club amid Man Utd links») Agostino Gemito/PA Wire/dpa Antonio Conte says he is not in advanced negotiations with any club after being linked with taking over as manager of Manchester United. Reports in his native Italy suggested former Chelsea and Tottenham boss Conte has set out conditions for his services, including over transfer policy as well as salary demands, should United decide to replace under-fire head coach Michael Carrick. Conte guided Napoli to the Scudetto in 2025, but left the club at the end of last season after finishing runners-up to Inter. The 57-year-old posted a statement, in both Italian and English, on his Instagram story stressing he would only consider a return to management when he believed "the conditions are right". Conte said: "Following recent media reports in Italy and abroad, I feel it is appropriate to clarify my position. "My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage. "Following a wonderful and successful spell in charge of Napoli, I will take the time I need to consider how and when to return to management. It will be a carefully considered decision, one I will make when I believe the conditions are right. "I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my 'strong personality'. These reports are unfounded, as there is currently no concrete basis for such assessments. "Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager. "Until then, any assumptions about my demands and my professional future remain speculation and cannot be treated as fact."

item.title: Michael Carrick is '100%' confident he can turn around Man Utd form
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick reacts following the UEFA Champions League match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium. (is associated with: «Michael Carrick is '100%' confident he can turn around Man Utd form») Luca Rossini/PA Wire/dpa Michael Carrick is 100% certain he can turn things around at Manchester United after the under-fire manager began his press conference with an emotional speech about the state of the club. The 45-year-old's position is hanging in the balance after Wednesday's calamitous 4-1 Champions League loss at Como extended their winless to a seventh match in all competitions - the club's worse run of form since 2015. Carrick will take charge of Sunday's return to Premier League action at home to Bournemouth but there is a sense that it may only prove a stay of execution for the United head coach. But the former midfielder will not go down without a fight and began Friday's press conference with a defiant five-minute speech, admitting "we've kind of lost our way a little bit" but "we'll get it back". "There's always conversations going on," Carrick said when he faced his first question. "I think it's pretty obvious how we're all feeling. "The responsibility for me to be in this position is to lead. It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, what we are as a group and what we look like and what we feel like. "If anything, to hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry. You know, that's the position I'm in, and it's a privileged position. "Discussions are going on, getting the players in a good frame of mind and well organised to put in a good performance on Sunday." Asked if he is convinced he can still turn things around at United, Carrick said: "Yeah, yeah, 100%."

item.title: 'Double standard': Özil wants football sanctions against Russia lifted
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Former German national team player Mesut Ozil (C) stands in the stands behind Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan (front row, 2nd R) and his wife, Emine Erdogan (front row, 2nd L), during the UEFA Euro 2024 soccer match between the Netherlands and Turkey at Berlin’s Olympic Stadium. (is associated with: «'Double standard': Özil wants football sanctions against Russia lifted») Marcus Brandt/dpa Former Germany midfielder Mesut Özil has called on footballl authorities to end sanctions against Russia, accusing them of double standard because Israel has not been banned. World governing body FIFA and Europe's UEFA have banned Russian teams from international events since the start of Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Israel has been criticised over the military operation in Gaza it started after the Hamas group attacked Israel in October 2023. It is not been sanctioned by football authorities. Özil, who helped Germany win the World Cup in 2014, spoke out on the sidelines of a veterans' game between his former Turkish club Başakşehir and Russian side Zenit St Petersburg earlier in the week. "I'd like to say this: football has always brought peace. As long as we don't focus on race or religion, the world of sport has always brought people together," he said. "As is well known, and as you know, FIFA has not imposed any sanctions on Israeli teams, but it has done so against Russian teams. "Here, I would like to appeal, as they say, to FIFA. Hopefully, they will stop applying double standards and treat everyone equally. That is why I would like to thank you all for organising this event." Özil has supported the Palestinian case in the past, including two years ago on Instagram where he posted a map with the name Israel crossed out and Palestine written underneath. Germany-born Özil played for Schalke, Werder Bremen, Real Madrid, Arsenal, Fenerbahçe and Başakşehir, where he ended his career in 2023. He won 92 Germany caps but retired from the team in 2018 over a controversy around a picture that showed him with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

item.title: How UC Bearcats Week 8 matchup with Brendan Sorsby fell apart
item.description: When the Big 12 released its 2026 football schedule, Week 8 immediately stood out for Cincinnati fans. The Bearcats were set to host Texas Tech and former quarterback Brendan Sorsby after his transfer to the Red Raiders . Sorsby transferred after two seasons at Cincinnati , and was one of the most sought-after prospects in the portal. He ultimately landed with the Red Raiders , who were coming off a 2025 College Football Playoff berth. His decision to leave the Bearcats prompted the university to sue Sorsby for a $1 million buyout after he allegedly violated his multi-year NIL revenue-sharing agreement. CFP contenders and pretenders: Race just got flipped upside down. Here’s who leads now Of course, Sorsby's reunion with Cincinnati is no longer in play — and not because of an injury. Sorsby is no longer on Texas Tech's roster after he and Texas Tech mutually agreed to part ways following a high-profile NCAA gambling investigation involving the former Indiana and Cincinnati signal-caller. Here's what to know about why Sorsby left Texas Tech before the season even started: Why is Brendan Sorsby no longer on Texas Tech's roster? Sorsby and Texas Tech parted ways on June 15 after the Big 12 Conference filed a federal lawsuit in Dallas seeking the authority to sanction the school if he played for the Red Raiders. The move came after a Texas judge granted Sorsby a temporary injunction that restored his eligibility while he remained under NCAA investigation related to a gambling addiction. "I am grateful for the support from my family, my Tech coaching staff, teammates, the community, and so many others who have encouraged me to address and learn more about this important issue," Sorsby wrote in a post on Instagram. "As my journey continues, I remain fully committed to and focused on being the best I can be, both on and off the field." Sorsby declared for the 2026 NFL Supplemental Draft, though the league declined to host for the former college quarterback. As it stands, he cannot enter the league until the 2027 draft. Brendan Sorsby betting controversy, explained The NCAA in March received a tip about Sorsby’s betting activity from an online gambling book, which had been informed by law enforcement. On April 27 the Red Raiders announced Sorsby was checking himself into a residential treatment program in Arizona for a gambling addiction that dated back to his true freshman season at Indiana in 2022. That season, Sorsby placed bets for the first eight games of the season, when he was a member of the Hoosiers' scout team. He announced on May 28 that he had completed a 35-day inpatient rehab program in Arizona. The NCAA denied Sorsby's request for reinstatement for the 2026 season on May 26, which led him to file an injunction against the NCAA in Lubbock County. item.content:encoded: When the Big 12 released its 2026 football schedule, Week 8 immediately stood out for Cincinnati fans. The Bearcats were set to host Texas Tech and former quarterback Brendan Sorsby after his transfer to the Red Raiders . Sorsby transferred after two seasons at Cincinnati , and was one of the most sought-after prospects in the portal. He ultimately landed with the Red Raiders , who were coming off a 2025 College Football Playoff berth. His decision to leave the Bearcats prompted the university to sue Sorsby for a $1 million buyout after he allegedly violated his multi-year NIL revenue-sharing agreement. CFP contenders and pretenders: Race just got flipped upside down. Here’s who leads now Of course, Sorsby's reunion with Cincinnati is no longer in play — and not because of an injury. Sorsby is no longer on Texas Tech's roster after he and Texas Tech mutually agreed to part ways following a high-profile NCAA gambling investigation involving the former Indiana and Cincinnati signal-caller. Here's what to know about why Sorsby left Texas Tech before the season even started: Why is Brendan Sorsby no longer on Texas Tech's roster? Sorsby and Texas Tech parted ways on June 15 after the Big 12 Conference filed a federal lawsuit in Dallas seeking the authority to sanction the school if he played for the Red Raiders. The move came after a Texas judge granted Sorsby a temporary injunction that restored his eligibility while he remained under NCAA investigation related to a gambling addiction. "I am grateful for the support from my family, my Tech coaching staff, teammates, the community, and so many others who have encouraged me to address and learn more about this important issue," Sorsby wrote in a post on Instagram. "As my journey continues, I remain fully committed to and focused on being the best I can be, both on and off the field." Sorsby declared for the 2026 NFL Supplemental Draft, though the league declined to host for the former college quarterback. As it stands, he cannot enter the league until the 2027 draft. Brendan Sorsby betting controversy, explained The NCAA in March received a tip about Sorsby’s betting activity from an online gambling book, which had been informed by law enforcement. On April 27 the Red Raiders announced Sorsby was checking himself into a residential treatment program in Arizona for a gambling addiction that dated back to his true freshman season at Indiana in 2022. That season, Sorsby placed bets for the first eight games of the season, when he was a member of the Hoosiers' scout team. He announced on May 28 that he had completed a 35-day inpatient rehab program in Arizona. The NCAA denied Sorsby's request for reinstatement for the 2026 season on May 26, which led him to file an injunction against the NCAA in Lubbock County. Bowl Projections: Week 7 upsets impact college football bowl projections with CFP field shuffling The injunction revealed that Sorsby had placed more than $90,000 in bets over four years through accounts registered to the names of family members and friends. Those wagers included at least 40 bets on Indiana when he was a member of the Hoosiers, but also included bets placed on professional sports . The documents also revealed that, since transferring to Texas Tech, Sorsby sent approximately $5,000 through Venmo or Zelle to an unnamed individual who placed bets on his behalf. College football risers and fallers: BYU is for real. Alabama, Texas in trouble His injunction to play for Texas Tech was granted on June 8 by Judge Ken Curry of the 99th District Court of Lubbock County: a decision that merely imposed a two-game suspension on Sorsby for Texas Tech's first two games of the season against Abilene Christian and Oregon State. That decision led to an uproar from across the country, with several athletic directors coming out publicly and stating they would not allow their programs to schedule Texas Tech in future contests. It also led to the Big 12 Conference filing a complaint in federal court seeking a declaratory judgment that would allow the league to enforce its bylaws and potentially sanction Texas Tech should the Red Raiders play Sorsby. The Big 12 considered sanctioning Texas Tech if it played Sorsby, in turn resulting in a legal threat from Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton if the conference tried to enforce its rules. Attorneys general in Oklahoma, Kansas and Utah responded, saying they would back up the conference, which ultimately sued Texas Tech in a Dallas court. Eventually, Sorsby and Texas Tech agreed to part ways as he prepared for the NFL supplemental draft. The NFL announced in June it would not hold a supplemental draft in 2026, blocking a path for Sorsby to compete in the NFL in 2026. Is Cincinnati under investigation by the NCAA for Brendan Sorbsy? No. The NCAA inquiry into University of Cincinnati Athletics regarding Sorsby's gambling was closed on Sept. 2 with no punishments issued to the Bearcats. Sorsby’s agent, Ron Slavin, claimed in a Dallas radio interview in June that Cincinnati knew about Sorsby’s gambling activity and did not act on it. Cincinnati, however, denied the accusation, saying in a statement that had it known of any impermissible gambling, it would have reported it to the NCAA. "Earlier this summer, NCAA enforcement staff completed an inquiry into a former Cincinnati student-athlete’s prohibited betting activity during his time at the university. The inquiry is now closed, and the student-athlete was found to have committed a Level III violation," UC Senior Associate Athletic Director for Communications Zach Stipe said in a statement to The Cincinnati Enquirer, part of the USA TODAY Network, on Sept. 2. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: How UC Bearcats Week 8 matchup with Brendan Sorsby fell apart

item.title: Lamborghini Super Trofeo |Europe, Race 2: Salonen/Tuomaala take the win, Iaquinta/Gilardoni crowned champions
item.description: Motorsport photo Matias Salonen and Henri Tuomaala claimed victory in the second encounter of the Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europe at Monza, a race that saw Kevin Gilardoni and Simone Iaquinta crowned 2026 PRO class champions. The race was highly eventful, complicated by a persistent, intermittent drizzle that began to fall on the Monza asphalt just minutes before the start. During the formation lap, Patrik Fraboni (Oregon Team) hit the wall exiting the 'Ascari' chicane, ending his title hopes and effectively sealing the championship for Iaquinta and Gilardoni. The first half of the race was characterised by the Safety Car. After a few laps of green-flag racing, it was deployed once again following off-track excursions by Alessio Ruffini (ASR), Philip Tang (DL Racing), and Euan Hankey (VSR). It remained on track until 22 minutes from the end, coinciding with the opening of the pit-stop window. Following the initial lead held by Marzio Moretti ahead of Nicolas Stati, the classification shifted significantly during the round of pit stops, as teams—including those that had started on rain tyres—switched to dry-weather rubber. The #88 Huracán driven by Tuomaala and Salonen surged into the lead; having started in sixth position, their climb through the field secured a one-two finish for Leipert Motorsport, with Stati and Leitch taking second place overall. Rounding out the podium were Berreby and Giraud in the Villorba-entered Huracán, followed by their teammates Strignano and Pujatti, while Leitzke Grotta and Spina (Oregon Team) fought their way into the top five. Moretti and Paolo Biglieri dropped to sixth, but they were able to celebrate victory in the PRO/AM class, finishing ahead of Cristovao/Levet (VSR) and Astafjev/Cecotto (Invictus Corse), who took ninth and tenth place overall. Positioned ahead of them were Jerzy Spinkiewicz (Uniq Racing) and the duo of Volfe/Balestriero (Leipert Motorsport). Iaquinta and Gilardoni, who started from the back of the grid due to a fuel pump issue encountered during Qualifying 2, managed to fight their way up to 14th place, but were handed a 10-second penalty for a pit-stop infringement. Despite a spin at the 'Roggia' chicane, Andrzej Lewandowski secured the win in the AM class behind the wheel of his ASR-entered Huracán, finishing ahead of Knoll/Kuppens (Micanek Motorsport) and Lémeret/Gillion (CMR). In the Lamborghini Cup class, Claude-Yves Gosselin (Villorba Corse) got the better of Ostergaard/Moller Demant (DC Motorsport)—who were crowned category champions—following a hard-fought second half of the race, with Adalberto Baptista (Oregon) coming in third. Lamborghini Super Trofeo Europa - Monza: classifica Gara 2 To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Xabi Alonso provides Emi Martinez timeline after horror head injury
item.description: Xabi Alonso has provided a timeline for Emi Martinez’s return after the Chelsea goalkeeper suffered a horror head injury in the 2-0 win at Everton last weekend. Martinez was rushed to hospital after a sickening collision with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite , clashing heads as Martinez came off his line to collect an aerial cross. The Argentinian received oxygen on the pitch and was eventually carried off on a stretcher more than eight minutes after the collision. Alonso confirmed after the match that the goalkeeper was conscious. Martinez underwent successful surgery after the clash, sharing an update from his hospital bed on Instagram to say he expects to be “back in a few weeks”. And Alonso has now provided more a positive update on Martinez’s recovery, saying: “He’s doing better. He had the surgery and day by day he’s feeling better but we still need to wait. “Few weeks. Hopefully less than more but we need to wait. The good thing is he’s feeling better. He needs to listen to the opinion of the doctors and his surgeons but considering that it was a bad one, he’s doing good.” Martinez’s absence opens up an opportunity for second-choice goalkeeper Mike Penders, 21, to get an extended run in the side, which will start when Chelsea host struggling Tottenham in a London derby on Saturday. The Belgian, who spent last season on loan at sister club Strasbourg , made his Premier League debut off the bench at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last week and Alonso is confident he is ready to step into the limelight. Mike Penders will come into the side for an extended run amid Martinez's absence (Getty) “He’s ready,” said Alonso. “He’s been training well, he’s played a couple of cup games where he’s showed he has a good level. “When he came on against Everton, he showed his personality, his qualities, so that’s why we have a squad to be ready for these kind of situations and we are fully convinced that Mike can play very well.” Penders has had comparisons to countryman and former Chelsea stopper Thibaut Courtois, something that Alonso very much recognises. "A lot [of similarities],” he said. “Not just the nationality, but the stature, both-footed, both dominant in the air. I spoke with Thibaut as well at the World Cup asking about Mike. He said himself he could see resemblances with Mike. “We need to help him and support him, but he is the keeper for the present and the future.”

item.title: North Wales Crusaders set for RFL talks over future
item.description: A previous incarnation of Crusaders played in Super League between 2009 and 2011 [BBC] North Wales Crusaders officials are to hold talks with the Rugby Football League (RFL) in a bid to save the club. Crusaders withdrew from the process of bidding for a licence for 2027 earlier this week. The RFL have said the club had been unable to satisfy their requests for next year. The governing body have been looking for Crusaders to deposit £150,000 in an escrow account to prove financial funding is in place. Crusaders will present a revised business plan when they meet RFL officials later on Friday. Chairman Jamie Elkaleh said the club had received "overwhelmingly positive and supportive" messages following the announcement. Rugby league's record loss but Crusaders win survival Brewery Field to become Crusaders' permanent home Wales' only professional rugby league side had been on the brink of collapse earlier this year when the owners announced they would no longer provide funding, only months after they had won the League One title. A group of supporters and volunteers rallied and a new company, NW Rugby League 26 Ltd, was formed and granted an interim licence by the RFL. The club was deducted 12 points as punishment for its financial failings, and completed the 2026 season with a hastily reassembled squad. Crusaders finished bottom of the Championship, losing 21 of their 24 games. Their 134-0 defeat by London Broncos in June was the biggest loss of any side in the top two divisions in the 131-year history of rugby league.

item.title: Bukayo Saka injury ‘not good’ as Arsenal face nervous wait
item.description: Arsenal are still yet to discover the extent of Bukayo Saka ’s thigh injury but Mikel Arteta has admitted the early signs are “not good”. The England international pulled up with the issue in the first half of the 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday. Saka is set to undergo further assessment ahead of Arsenal’s home match against Everton on Saturday. Bukayo Saka leaves the pitch after incurring an injury (Adam Davy/PA) (PA Wire) But he did not train on Friday and Arsenal face a nervous wait before discovering how long he could be sidelined for. “He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury,” Arteta said. "We will know more probably tomorrow. We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists. "Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch and is struggling to walk without any pain and is restricted to movement, they are not good signs. “So let's be very patient so we can give a definitive assessment, and then let you know." Saka’s injury means Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze will have the opportunity to start against Everton. Madueke scored Arsenal’s winner at Nottingham Forest last Sunday while Eze was on target in the draw at the Allianz Arena in midweek. With forward Christos Tzolis also sidelined, Madueke and Eze will be given additional responsibility for leading Arsenal’s attack. Saka missed several stretches of the past two seasons due to a mixture of muscle injuries - dealing with hamstring, thigh and hip problems. Saka went down unopposed before limping off in Munich (Reuters) The 25-year-old was also affected by an Achilles injury over the final stretch of last season, which impacted his fitness at the summer’s World Cup. Arsenal play five times before the November international break and travel to Liverpool in the Premier League next weekend. Following Saturday’s home game against Everton, there are also trips to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup and Slavia Prague in the Champions League. They conclude the stretch of fixtures by hosting Hull in the Premier League on 7 November ahead of the two-week international window.

item.title: PREVIEW | Crystal Palace vs Newcastle: team news, lineups, predictions (Premier League 25/10)
item.description: PREVIEW | Crystal Palace vs Newcastle: team news, lineups, predictions (Premier League 25/10) Crystal Palace and Newcastle clash this Sunday at the Selhurst Park for matchweek eight of the Premier League . The match will be broadcast live at 14:00 on Sky Sports Football. Crystal Palace have won 7 points to date and are placed in 14th position. In their last outing, Pierre Sage 's team drew 2-2 against Besiktas (UEFA Europa League 2026/27). Newcastle have won 8 points to date and are placed in 11th position. In their last game, Matthias Jaissle 's team lost 0-1 against Aston Villa (Premier League 2026/27). The last meeting between the two teams ended with Crystal Palace winning 2-1 . item.title: Pros and Cons: Should the Mets sign Teruaki Sato?
item.description: The last time the Mets made a big splash by signing a position player from Japan was the only time they made a big splash signing a position player from Japan. It was the 2003-04 offseason, and the player was Kaz Matsui , a power-hitting superstar infielder. The signing of Matsui was enormous at the time since it came on the heels of Ichiro Suzuki being the first-ever Japanese position player to be posted and signed by an MLB team -- in 2001 with the Mariners, when he won the MVP award. Shortly after Suzuki arrived, Hideki Matsui inked a deal with the Yankees during the 2002-03 offseason and made an immediate impact in the majors. The Mets had signed a Japanese position player before, landing the flashy outfielder Tsuyoshi Shinjo ahead of the 2001 season. But Shinjo, while a fun player, was not viewed as a difference-maker. Kaz Matsui was, though he didn't live up to the hype. He had a respectable .727 OPS in 2004 but flamed out quickly in New York, with a .670 OPS in 255 games over parts of three seasons before he was traded to Colorado in June of 2006. Matsui had some solid years for the Rockies and Astros later in his career, but never hit more than nine home runs in a season -- a massive disappointment after blasting 30-plus homers in back-to-back seasons for the Seibu Lions in Japan before coming to the majors. Since Matsui, the Mets have been active in the Japanese market, but it has been limited to pitchers -- most recently the signing of Kodai Senga and strong pursuit of Yoshinobu Yamamoto before he landed with the Dodgers. Meanwhile, Japanese position players have continued to wind up elsewhere. Most recently, Shohei Ohtani went to the Angels and then the Dodgers (refusing to even consider an East Coast team), Seiya Suzuki signed with the Cubs, Kazuma Okamoto landed with the Blue Jays, and Munetaka Murakami inked a deal with the White Sox. Another crop of Japanese stars is about to hit the open market this offseason, and slugging infielder Teruaki Sato could be a strong fit for New York. Should the Mets pursue Sato? item.content:encoded: The last time the Mets made a big splash by signing a position player from Japan was the only time they made a big splash signing a position player from Japan. It was the 2003-04 offseason, and the player was Kaz Matsui , a power-hitting superstar infielder. The signing of Matsui was enormous at the time since it came on the heels of Ichiro Suzuki being the first-ever Japanese position player to be posted and signed by an MLB team -- in 2001 with the Mariners, when he won the MVP award. Shortly after Suzuki arrived, Hideki Matsui inked a deal with the Yankees during the 2002-03 offseason and made an immediate impact in the majors. The Mets had signed a Japanese position player before, landing the flashy outfielder Tsuyoshi Shinjo ahead of the 2001 season. But Shinjo, while a fun player, was not viewed as a difference-maker. Kaz Matsui was, though he didn't live up to the hype. He had a respectable .727 OPS in 2004 but flamed out quickly in New York, with a .670 OPS in 255 games over parts of three seasons before he was traded to Colorado in June of 2006. Matsui had some solid years for the Rockies and Astros later in his career, but never hit more than nine home runs in a season -- a massive disappointment after blasting 30-plus homers in back-to-back seasons for the Seibu Lions in Japan before coming to the majors. Since Matsui, the Mets have been active in the Japanese market, but it has been limited to pitchers -- most recently the signing of Kodai Senga and strong pursuit of Yoshinobu Yamamoto before he landed with the Dodgers. Meanwhile, Japanese position players have continued to wind up elsewhere. Most recently, Shohei Ohtani went to the Angels and then the Dodgers (refusing to even consider an East Coast team), Seiya Suzuki signed with the Cubs, Kazuma Okamoto landed with the Blue Jays, and Munetaka Murakami inked a deal with the White Sox. Another crop of Japanese stars is about to hit the open market this offseason, and slugging infielder Teruaki Sato could be a strong fit for New York. Should the Mets pursue Sato? Here are the pros and cons... Mar 15, 2025; Bunkyo, Tokyo, Japan; Hanshin Tigers right fielder Teruaki Sato (8) gestures during the fifth inning against the Chicago Cubs at Tokyo Dome. / Darren Yamashita - Imagn Images PROS Sato has reached another level offensively over the last two seasons for the Hanshin Tigers. He smacked 40 homers and 34 doubles while posting a .924 OPS in 2025 as he won the Central League MVP award. Sato followed that up in 2026 with another monster season. In 143 games, he slashed .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs, 40 doubles, 100 runs scored, and 106 RBI -- winning the Triple Crown in the process. Sato also excelled in a small sample against international competition in the 2026 World Baseball Classic, hitting .300/.417/.600 with three doubles in 12 plate appearances. A look at Sato's advanced stats don't reveal any glaring issues. While he has a propensity to strike out (he fanned 164 times in 143 games in 2026), his strikeout percentage has been quite steady since 2023 -- and it actually ticked down a bit from 2025 (27.3 percent) to 2026 (26.7 percent) as his power output increased. Sato's BABIP in 2026 (.370) was a career high, so there should be some regression there. But his BABIP has always trended relatively high (.343 in 2024, .323 in 2025). When it comes to durability, Sato has been a rock of sorts, appearing in 132 or more games in each of his first six seasons. Sato also has youth on his side, as he'll be playing the entire 2027 season at just 28 years old. While Sato has been primarily a third baseman and corner outfielder in Japan, many experts believe his defensive home in the majors will be at first base. If Sato is indeed destined for first base, it would make him an ideal fit for a Mets team that still has a huge hole at the position. Jared Young performed admirably there this past season with Jorge Polanco injured and Mark Vientos ineffective, but Young -- who doesn't have much power and struggles against left-handed pitching -- might profile better in a reserve role. Mar 15, 2025; Bunkyo, Tokyo, Japan; Hanshin Tigers right fielder Teruaki Sato (8) poses for a photo after defeating the Chicago Cubs at Tokyo Dome. / Darren Yamashita - Imagn Images CONS While Sato might fit better at first base than third base, that doesn't mean he can definitely handle the position. At the same time, plenty of players have made a successful transition across the diamond, so there should be hope that a relatively athletic player like Sato can do it. Another possible knock against Sato -- strictly when it comes to a possible Mets pursuit -- is that he hits from the left side of the plate. The Mets are already very left-handed, with Juan Soto , Carson Benge , and A.J. Ewing among their key offensive cogs. But they do have some variety with the switch-hitting Francisco Lindor , both of their catchers ( Francisco Alvarez and Luis Torrens ), and Bo Bichette (if he opts in to his contract) all hitting from the right side. Then there's the strikeouts. As is noted above, Sato's strikeout rate for Hanshin in 2026 was 26.7 percent (164 K's in 143 games). In 2024, in what was his last full season playing in Japan, Murakami's strikeout rate was 29.5 percent (180 in 143 games). In 69 games in 2025, Murakami's strikeout rate was 28.6 percent (71 in 69 games). In his first season for the White Sox, Murakami fanned a whopping 196 times in 127 games -- a rate of 35.4 percent. Even though it's fair to expect Sato's strikeout rate to tick up as he transitions to the majors, there's no reason to believe it will be as stark as Murakami's increase. In any event, even while striking out as often as he did in 2026, Murakami was still very valuable for Chicago, posting an .825 OPS (130 OPS+) and cracking 35 homers in 127 games. VERDICT With the Mets seemingly locked in at most positions on the diamond, the easiest way to move the needle offensively is to add someone to play first base or be the regular designated hitter. And with there being serious drawbacks to adding a DH-only player, the target should be first base. There are other intriguing first basemen set to be on the free agent market, including Ty France . But none of them possess the upside of Sato. Sato obviously comes with some risk, but it's time for the Mets to take a big swing on a high upside talent.

item.title: NBA Power Rankings: All 15 Eastern Conference teams ranked in opening week
item.description: The NBA has finally returned, and the Eastern Conference is already proving to be unpredictable. In just three days, the reigning champs have fallen, a flurry of blowouts took place, and contenders scrapped against each other for their first wins. There’s plenty to unpack from week one, but these early power rankings display the parity among the East. MORE: 4 NBA teams that will surprise in 2026-27 season Ranks 15-11 Sep 28, 2026; Brooklyn, NY, USA; Brooklyn Nets forward-center Julius Randle (30) talks with media at Brooklyn Nets HSS Training Center. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 15. Brooklyn Nets 0-1 Brooklyn lost its home opener to Charlotte. Both Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle played well, with Randle putting up 33 points and MPJ adding 26. Both players shot efficiently, but it wasn’t enough to get the Nets a win. Brooklyn is a young team with plenty of room to grow, but it has a long way to go. 14. Chicago Bulls 0-1 The Bulls were blown out by Toronto in their season opener. Playing on the road against a very good team is a tough environment, but it’s still concerning that Chicago trailed by as many as 48 points. With a revamped roster and front office, the Bulls are a young team that will likely need some time to grow. 13. Milwaukee Bucks 0-1 The Bucks lost to the Washington Wizards on the road in their season opener. Tyler Herro and Jaime Jaquez Jr. led the way, each putting up more than 20 points. Milwaukee looked better than expected, especially considering it was an away game. However, losing to Washington is still concerning, given that the Wizards aren’t expected to be very good this season. 12. Charlotte Hornets 1-0 Charlotte took down the Brooklyn Nets in New York to open its season. No one player stood out, as multiple Hornets finished with around 20 points. Beating what could be the worst team in the conference isn’t necessarily impressive, but getting the job done on the road is still a solid start for Charlotte. 11. Orlando Magic 0-1 Orlando lost to Atlanta in its home opener despite a phenomenal performance from Paolo Banchero. Banchero finished with 35 points, seven rebounds and 10 assists while missing just two shots. The Magic played well but still came up short, which is concerning for a team with high expectations entering the season. Top 10 Oct 8, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Washington Wizards forward Anthony Davis (23) is defended by New York Knicks guard Josh Hart (3) during the first quarter at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Alexander Wohl-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 10. Washington Wizards 1-0 The Wizards took down the Milwaukee Bucks in their home opener, winning by 12 points. However, beating a struggling Milwaukee team at home isn’t the most convincing way to start the season. Anthony Davis led the way with 34 points, while Trae Young added 20 points and 13 assists. Washington got the job done

Mandatory Credit: Alexander Wohl-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) 10. Washington Wizards 1-0 The Wizards took down the Milwaukee Bucks in their home opener, winning by 12 points. However, beating a struggling Milwaukee team at home isn’t the most convincing way to start the season. Anthony Davis led the way with 34 points, while Trae Young added 20 points and 13 assists. Washington got the job done, but it will need to prove itself against tougher competition. 9. Indiana Pacers 1-0 Tyrese Haliburton made his return to the court as the Pacers opened their season against the New Orleans Pelicans. Indiana escaped with a three-point win in a nail-biter. Pascal Siakam led the way with 35 points, while Haliburton finished with 23 points and 12 assists. If Haliburton can return to form, Indiana could be a team to watch in the Eastern Conference. 8. Atlanta Hawks 1-0 Atlanta took down the Orlando Magic on the road to open its season. The Hawks were led by an unlikely 31-point performance from Nickeil Alexander-Walker. Jalen Johnson and Dyson Daniels also chipped in 20 points apiece. Atlanta earned an impressive road win against a team with playoff aspirations, giving the Hawks an encouraging start to the season. 7. Miami Heat 0-1 Miami was manhandled by the Minnesota Timberwolves in its season opener. The Heat have some talented pieces, but this roster doesn’t appear to be built for a championship run. With Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo in the mix, Miami has the potential to be a difficult matchup for opposing teams. However, the Heat have plenty to prove after their opening-night performance. 6. Boston Celtics 0-1 Boston lost its season opener against Detroit in a game that raised some early concerns. Surprisingly, Paul George looked like the best offseason signing in the league, putting up 38 points in an impressive performance. Meanwhile, Mitchell Robinson struggled to make an impact, raising questions about his fit. Jayson Tatum also had an ugly shooting night, going 6-for-23 from the field. Boston has plenty of talent, but it will need more consistency to compete with the East’s best. MORE: Ranking top 7 NBA rookies entering 2026-27 season Top 5 Oct 21, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, CAN; Toronto Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard (2) dribbles against the Chicago Bulls during the second quarter at Scotiabank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images 5. Toronto Raptors 1-0 Toronto blew out Chicago in its season opener, establishing itself as a team to watch early in the season. The Bulls aren’t a terrible roster on paper, making the Raptors’ performance even more impressive. Toronto led by as many as 48 points, while four players finished with at least 20 points. It was a dominant showing from a team looking to make some noise in the Eastern Conference. 4. Cleveland Cavaliers 0-1 Cleveland lost to Philadelphia in its season opener, but playing on the road against one of the conference’s top teams is no easy task. Donovan Mitchell and Tyrese Maxey matched each other with 32 points apiece in an entertaining matchup. The Cavaliers have the talent to compete with the East’s best, but they’ll need to bounce back after a tough opening-night loss. 3. Detroit Pistons 1-0 Detroit opened its season with an impressive win over a talented Boston Celtics team at home. Cade Cunningham led the way, while Jalen Duren looked great after a lackluster playoff performance last season. The Pistons made a statement by taking down one of the conference’s top teams, giving fans reason to be optimistic about what’s ahead. 2. New York Knicks 0-1 The Knicks lost at home to what could be the best team in the league. Despite the loss, New York didn’t look bad, but Philadelphia proved to be too much. The Knicks have the talent to compete with anyone in the Eastern Conference, and one loss against a championship contender shouldn’t change that. Still, they’ll need to bounce back quickly to keep pace with the conference’s best. 1. Philadelphia 76ers 2-0 The Philadelphia 76ers have wasted no time making a statement with their new-look roster featuring LeBron James and Jaylen Brown. Philadelphia took down the Knicks in New York before returning home to defeat the Cleveland Cavaliers in its second game. Starting the season 2-0 with wins over two of the East’s top teams is an impressive way to open the year. If Philadelphia can maintain this level of play, it could be the team to beat in the Eastern Conference. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Knicks used empty promises of championship rings to trick employees into clicking a phishing link
item.description: Knicks used empty promises of championship rings to trick employees into clicking a phishing link originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Knicks danced in confetti in June, relishing their first title in a generation off the backs of Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mike Brown and more. Four months on, a lot of the goodwill that seemed to fall at the feet of New York owner James Dolan for his willingness to bankroll that title-winning unit appears to have vanished. The 71-year-old has drawn the ire of many basketball enthusiasts in recent decades. A Trump acolyte who was forced to settle a dispute with a former Knicks executive who alleged that he fired her after filing a sexual harassment report against former New York president Isiah Thomas, Dolan is hardly a popular figure in sports. He didn't do himself any favors with the his latest trick, one that saw him fool masses of Madison Square Garden employees hoping to get a chance to deck their fingers in gold after New York's championship triumph. Here's what you need to know about the Knicks phishing scandal that took social media by storm. MORE: Former ESPN personality, current Trump staffer throws beer on NBA fan Knicks championship ring cybersecurity test Dolan's passion for surveillance is well-documented at this point. Madison Square Garden has been less a sporting venue that a panopticon for Dolan, wrote Wired's Noah Shachtman and Robert Silverman in April 2026. The pairing, alongside investigative journalist Pablo Torre , helped reveal the extent of Dolan's obsession with cybersecurity, detailing how, among other things, Dolan's security staff harassed and "obsessively tracked" a trans woman over a two-year period. Perhaps it's unsurprising, then, to see Dolan and Co. return to the well once more, this time directing their efforts towards their own employees. Dolan's company picked quite the ruse as a trojan horse to pursue its obsession with biometrics. The Athletic's Joe Vardon detailed the scope of Dolan's fixation in an article that came out Thursday. Vardon reported that the Knicks governor reportedly sent an email to employees vowing to offer them the choice of a potential championship ring. item.content:encoded: Knicks used empty promises of championship rings to trick employees into clicking a phishing link originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Knicks danced in confetti in June, relishing their first title in a generation off the backs of Jalen Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mike Brown and more. Four months on, a lot of the goodwill that seemed to fall at the feet of New York owner James Dolan for his willingness to bankroll that title-winning unit appears to have vanished. The 71-year-old has drawn the ire of many basketball enthusiasts in recent decades. A Trump acolyte who was forced to settle a dispute with a former Knicks executive who alleged that he fired her after filing a sexual harassment report against former New York president Isiah Thomas, Dolan is hardly a popular figure in sports. He didn't do himself any favors with the his latest trick, one that saw him fool masses of Madison Square Garden employees hoping to get a chance to deck their fingers in gold after New York's championship triumph. Here's what you need to know about the Knicks phishing scandal that took social media by storm. MORE: Former ESPN personality, current Trump staffer throws beer on NBA fan Knicks championship ring cybersecurity test Dolan's passion for surveillance is well-documented at this point. Madison Square Garden has been less a sporting venue that a panopticon for Dolan, wrote Wired's Noah Shachtman and Robert Silverman in April 2026. The pairing, alongside investigative journalist Pablo Torre , helped reveal the extent of Dolan's obsession with cybersecurity, detailing how, among other things, Dolan's security staff harassed and "obsessively tracked" a trans woman over a two-year period. Perhaps it's unsurprising, then, to see Dolan and Co. return to the well once more, this time directing their efforts towards their own employees. Dolan's company picked quite the ruse as a trojan horse to pursue its obsession with biometrics. The Athletic's Joe Vardon detailed the scope of Dolan's fixation in an article that came out Thursday. Vardon reported that the Knicks governor reportedly sent an email to employees vowing to offer them the choice of a potential championship ring. MORE: Where Ty Jerome ranks for NBA MVP odds will leave basketball fans shocked "Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," the email read, per The Athletic. "[Employee name], this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you. "There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below." The email was a scam, however. The message was actually a phishing test, used to see if Madison Square Garden employees would click on the link featured at the bottom of the page. If they did, they were greeted not with jewelry, but with a mandatory cybersecurity class, per Vardon. MORE: Charles Oakley vs. James Dolan beef, explained Did Knicks employees actually get championship rings? Many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden employees are not expected to receive a championship ring for their troubles, per Vardon. Dolan has shown an unwillingness to part ways with his hordes of money over the years; ESPN's Shams Charania reported that New York's latest contract extension offer to star big Karl-Anthony Towns is worth more than $75 million less than he's eligible for. Dolan's unwillingness to give just rewards to players who have served his franchise dutifully appears to be a window into his frugality. Predictably, that stinginess is also reserved for mere mortals, including those that make up the masses of the Madison Square Garden workforce. Others subjected to the whims of the Dolan's parsimony appear to include select New York assistants, who have not yet received their signets. MORE: Donald Trump-James Dolan friendship, explained Online reaction to Knicks championship ring cybersecurity test Observers far and wide condemned Dolan and Co.'s actions on social media. Here are some of the more notable reactions to Dolan's controversial actions: This is kind of breaking my heart what a cruel thing to do in the face of joy — amanda (@jailedamanda) October 23, 2026 This is absolutely horrible and complete crap by the Knicks. Shame on them for not only holding the assistant coaches rings during the ceremony, but doing this with their employees. What a complete joke. — Brett Siegel (@BrettSiegelNBA) October 23, 2026 You have to be a truly terrible person to do this https://t.co/1v9Znnd3WG — Jeremy Schneider (@J_Schneider) October 23, 2026 Back in the day, we did a phishing test with a client who had recently removed free soda as an employee benefit. One of the things that our phishing email asked employees to log in and fill a survey about was if they would like to see free sodas returned to the workplace. The employees were so excited by the phishing email that they forwarded it around to each other to ensure that everybody got a copy and could log in and fill it out. Needless to say, the client was furious, and we all learned a very valuable lesson about running the content of the phishing emails by the client and their corporate communications team before sending it to their employees. — Joe Barrett (@BarrettJ) October 23, 2026 Nobody is saying “the Knicks should never do phishing tests.” We’re saying “teasing employees with information about rings they earned but may not receive is unnecessarily cruel.” Because it is. Have a shred of respect for the people who work for you. — Sam Quinn (@SamQuinnCBS) October 23, 2026 Do you know how pissed I would be…. my god. — Devin Newsom (@DevinNewsom) October 23, 2026 James Dolan won the title and called a crisis PR firm for an emergency strategy meeting to come up with new ways to demonstrate that he is still Evil — Rodger Sherman (@rodger) October 23, 2026 Knicks employees: “We getting championship rings?” James Dolan: https://t.co/SeiAo1r9gb — Josiah Johnson (@KingJosiah54) October 23, 2026 MORE : Ranking the greatest Knicks of all time

item.title: Lions Pegged as Trade Landing Spot for $111 Million DT
item.description: Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. Getty Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. Getty Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes should have defensive players on his radar before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. Getty The Detroit Lions could really use an upgrade at cornerback at the NFL trade deadline. But that hasn’t stopped pundits from linking the Lions to defensive playmakers at other positions. This week, Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame called the Lions one of the two best potential fits for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. “Slated to hit free agency after this season, Payne is a fascinating player to watch. At 29, he hasn’t had more than four sacks or 11 quarterback hits since 2022, the lone time he was a Pro Bowler,” wrote Verderame. “Still, he’s an impact player on the inside who commands double teams, logging at least 61% of the snaps every year of his career. “If Washington makes Payne available, expect a market to develop.” Payne has 14 combined tackles, including two tackles for loss and five quarterback hits this season. He also has one sack and one forced fumble. The veteran defensive lineman could be on the move before the deadline because the Commanders sit at 1-4-1 entering their bye this week. Payne has earned $111.8 million during his NFL career according to Spotrac . Why Commanders DT Daron Payne Could Fit With Lions Getty Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. The Lions enter Week 7 last in total defense and pass defense. They are also second-to-last in third-down percentage allowed and yet, the Lions are first in sacks. Those statistics point to Detroit needing a cornerback. Based on the eye test, Lions fans everywhere would likely agree. The team planned to have former first-round pick Terrion Arnold on the roster this season. They then didn’t really replace him when the team released Arnold following his legal trouble over the summer. Yet, some pundits are still proposing the Lions acquire a defensive lineman. It’s not the worst idea, especially if Detroit makes multiple trades before the deadline to improve the defense. Payne would add a veteran presence to the team’s defensive line interior. That’s something the Lions lost this past offseason with the departures of D.J. Reader and Roy Lopez . Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 with a career-high 11.5 sacks, 18 tackles for loss and 20 quarterback hits. He also had five pass defenses that season. Since then, the lineman has just 12 sacks in 55 games. But he remains a reliable contributor along the interior. If it doesn’t take much draft capital, the Lions kicking the tires on acquiring Payne would make sense. Will Detroit GM Brad Holmes Make Aggressive NFL Trade Deadline Move? Ge

Getty Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. Getty The Detroit Lions could really use an upgrade at cornerback at the NFL trade deadline. But that hasn’t stopped pundits from linking the Lions to defensive playmakers at other positions. This week, Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame called the Lions one of the two best potential fits for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. “Slated to hit free agency after this season, Payne is a fascinating player to watch. At 29, he hasn’t had more than four sacks or 11 quarterback hits since 2022, the lone time he was a Pro Bowler,” wrote Verderame. “Still, he’s an impact player on the inside who commands double teams, logging at least 61% of the snaps every year of his career. “If Washington makes Payne available, expect a market to develop.” Payne has 14 combined tackles, including two tackles for loss and five quarterback hits this season. He also has one sack and one forced fumble. The veteran defensive lineman could be on the move before the deadline because the Commanders sit at 1-4-1 entering their bye this week. Payne has earned $111.8 million during his NFL career according to Spotrac . Why Commanders DT Daron Payne Could Fit With Lions Getty Sports Illustrated’s Matt Verderame named the Detroit Lions a potential fit for Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne. The Lions enter Week 7 last in total defense and pass defense. They are also second-to-last in third-down percentage allowed and yet, the Lions are first in sacks. Those statistics point to Detroit needing a cornerback. Based on the eye test, Lions fans everywhere would likely agree. The team planned to have former first-round pick Terrion Arnold on the roster this season. They then didn’t really replace him when the team released Arnold following his legal trouble over the summer. Yet, some pundits are still proposing the Lions acquire a defensive lineman. It’s not the worst idea, especially if Detroit makes multiple trades before the deadline to improve the defense. Payne would add a veteran presence to the team’s defensive line interior. That’s something the Lions lost this past offseason with the departures of D.J. Reader and Roy Lopez . Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 with a career-high 11.5 sacks, 18 tackles for loss and 20 quarterback hits. He also had five pass defenses that season. Since then, the lineman has just 12 sacks in 55 games. But he remains a reliable contributor along the interior. If it doesn’t take much draft capital, the Lions kicking the tires on acquiring Payne would make sense. Will Detroit GM Brad Holmes Make Aggressive NFL Trade Deadline Move? Getty Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes should have defensive players on his radar before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The question of whether the Lions could be in the market for someone like Payne greatly depends on how aggressive general manager Brad Holmes will be in the market. Being aggressive at the trade deadline isn’t typical for Holmes. Last season, the Lions didn’t make any significant trade deadline acquisitions. The year prior, they added one player through a notable trade — edge rusher Za’Darius Smith . If the Lions are only going to acquire one player again, it should be a cornerback. Payne is a nice to have, but he isn’t essential to trying to fix the Detroit defense. With Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams , the Lions have two quality starting defensive tackles. Dan Campbell has also regularly praised the team’s interior defensive line depth such as rookie Skyler Gill-Howard . The Lions have two and a half weeks to decide their trade deadline strategy. The league’s trade deadline is set for Tuesday, November 10. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Lions Pegged as Trade Landing Spot for $111 Million DT appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Daily Bean: Bruins Win; McDavid Makes History; Hellebuyck Suspension Ends Today
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Boston Bruins put up six for their sixth win in seven games. The Bruins cruised past the Nashville Predators last night, extending their point streak to seven games with a 6-0 win. Michael DiPietro made 28 saves for his first NHL shutout, but the night carried a little more meaning than that milestone. Elsewhere around the league, we’re seeing a lot of Connor. The one in Edmonton made history, while the one in Winnipeg (for now?) will see his suspension end today. There is a trade board, a report on a Blue Jackets left winger, and an update from Kyle Dubas on Ben Kindel. The Flyers may have some expendable trade pieces, and a couple of goalies made their debut last night. Happy Friday, catch up on Bruins and league news in today’s Daily Bean : Boston Bruins BRUINS WIN : The Bruins (8-2-1) extended their point streak to seven with a 6-0 thumping of the Nashville Predators (3-3-3). David Pastrnak scored twice, Charlie McAvoy finished with four assists, and Michael DiPietro made 28 saves for his first NHL shutout. Five different Bruins found the back of the net in the win. POSTGAME : Michael DiPietro’s first shutout came on a pretty meaningful night. The Bruins hosted Hockey Fights Cancer night on Thursday, and DiPietro, who lost his mother to cancer when he was five, spoke about what the milestone meant to him and his family. Ahead of warmups last night, the Bruins placed a jersey on their bench in memory of Alex Gimenez, the Bruins’ director of hockey operations, collective bargaining agreement, who passed away after a battle with cancer in September. In memory of our teammate, Alex Gimenez 💜 pic.twitter.com/J9oiGP9zF6 — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) October 22, 2026 NEXT UP : The Bruins have the day off today. They will hold a morning skate at TD Garden before closing the season series with San Jose tomorrow night. NHL News & National Hockey Now Sportsnet : Another night, another milestone for Connor McDavid . He’s up to 30 points in 10 games, becoming the fourth player in NHL history to hit that mark, joining Wayne Gretzky , Mario Lemieux , and Mike Bossy . He also had another five-point outing, and he and Lemieux are the only two players in league history to have three five-point nights in the first 10 games of a season. McDavid is on pace (and I say this very lightly) for 260 points this season. TSN : Today is the day Connor Hellebuyck ’s suspension is lifted, and he has to complete a physical in order to be restored to the active roster. The Jets play in the Heritage Classic on Sunday, and Darren Dreger reported that there could be an agreement to postpone Hellebuyck’s physical until after the game “out of respect to the Heritage Classic.” Sportsnet : Trade board! Why not? It’s still early, but Nick Kypreos released the second trade board of the season. Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin obviously dominate the headline, but a few Bruins (one current and two former) made it to the list. TSN : The Blue Jackets

item.title: Opelousas football outlast Cecilia in a Week 8 thriller between rivals
item.description: Every time Opelousas and Cecilia football face off, you'd better grab some popcorn. The 2026 meeting between the Tigers and Bulldogs was another production, as momentum shifted all night long in the Week 8 matchup. The Opelousas sideline went through a flurry of emotions with the lead changing countless time at Donald Garnder Staduim. Nearly 100 points scored later, the Tigers were the ones to come out on top, sneaking past the Bulldogs for a 50-48 victory. “This rivalry is rich, and we knew we had to help the seniors win this with this being the final home game of the regular season,” Opelousas running back Joseph Clues said. “We had to secure the win, and we just executed the plays that coach gave us.” It wasn’t a pretty victory for Opelousas, but it’ll go down as statement win, handing Cecilia its first loss in district play. With this win, the Tigers have now opened the doors for a possible three-way tie for the Class 4A District 5 championship. A chip on Opelousas’ shoulder Fans could tell Opelousas was eager to face off against Cecilia after last year’s disappointing loss. On Cecilia’s first offensive play of the drive, Opelousas senior Jaylon Owens landed a big hit on the Bulldogs quarterback, forcing a fumble. That set the tone for the rest of the night for the Tigers. Owens went on to be the Tigers’ leading receivers, tallying approximately 100 yards, a touchdown and three 2-point conversions. Whenever senior quarterback Collin Rideau needed an outlet, Owens was there along with senior Caden Arvie, who finished with approximately 80 yards receiving and a touchdown. The star of the Tigers' offense however, was Clues, who didn’t start the game due to being a bit banged up from last week. “He was nursing some injuries, but he gave me the sign that he was good to go,” Opelousas coach Harry Coleman said on Clues. “He warmed up real good, and he got out there and he showed what he is, man. He’s the workhorse of this team, and we’re gonna ride him.” Clues ran all night long, rushing for approximately 245 yards and four touchdowns on 28 carries. If the Bulldogs gave him a sliver of room, he squeezed through for big play after big play. While the Tigers had more penalties against them, the penalties against Cecilia proved more costly in such a close game. “We left a lot on the table, and I’m sure they think the same way, but just the little things that hurt us when it’s time,” Cecilia coach Cody Champange said. “If we would have caught the 2-point conversion, if we don’t muff the punt. We've got to clean those things up in a game like this.” In defeat, the Bulldogs never quit, with senior running back Deondre Briscoe l

item.title: OCS football defeats St. Fred's behind Tristan Raymond's strong outing
item.description: MONROE — Things started off slowly for Ouachita Christian in its District 2-1A opener at St. Frederick, but the Eagles had long since kicked things into gear by the end of the fourth quarter. As the 8-0 Eagles defeated St. Fred’s 51-7 on Thursday, Oct. 22, at Chip Luffey Field, ROCS junior Tristan Raymond continued to shine in his first year as starting quarterback. He totaled six touchdowns (four passing) for OCS as it rolled to another running-clock victory. “It’s just what Tristan does,” OCS junior D’Siah Bradshaw said. “All the hard work he puts into the summer, all the work he puts into the weight room on the field, those extra hours at practice, that's just hard work. It's not really surprising to me. I know what he’s capable of as a player and as a human being. He’s earned it, for sure.” LHSAA football: 4 storylines to watch for Week 8 in the Monroe area Added senior Jude Turner, “Tristan, that dude is an athlete. He’s blessed by God, and he’s got all kinds of talent. He makes us really, really good.” The Class 1A No. 1 Eagles gave up some chunk plays against the Warriors, including a long kickoff return in the third quarter by St. Fred’s senior JP Guerriero that set up the team’s only touchdown. One of Raymond’s passes was nearly picked off by a Warriors defender but caught by Eagles senior Hunter Oglesbee. There was tension between the two schools located 5 miles away from each other along Highway 165. "It's just a battle every year, and we knew it would be a night," OCS coach Steven Fitzhugh said. "(The Warriors have) come a long way since ( Bayou Jamb ), and they execute their scheme well running the option. (St. Fred's coach Tony) Osborne's done a good job with them, and (senior quarterback Michael) Malloy does a great job leading that entire offense. "They made plays on us (Thursday). Our defense, they bent, but they didn't break. Proud of the way our offense and defense executed and made plays and glad that our kids battled." Both Bradshaw and Turner had touchdown receptions for OCS against St. Fred's (2-5); Raymond hooked up with senior Luke Edwards twice in the endzone. Raymond now has 17 total touchdowns over his last three games. In addition to his four total touchdowns last week against Lincoln Prep , Raymond threw five touchdown passes on Oct. 9 against Bunkie. He said it's a "huge blessing" leading one of north Louisiana's top offenses. "(OCS offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach) Drew Vidrine does a great job with the schemes and the plays," Raymond said. "We've got great weapons around me, a great offensive line, so it's just the perfect recipe for success."
