item.content:encoded: MONROE — Things started off slowly for Ouachita Christian in its District 2-1A opener at St. Frederick, but the Eagles had long since kicked things into gear by the end of the fourth quarter. As the 8-0 Eagles defeated St. Fred’s 51-7 on Thursday, Oct. 22, at Chip Luffey Field, ROCS junior Tristan Raymond continued to shine in his first year as starting quarterback. He totaled six touchdowns (four passing) for OCS as it rolled to another running-clock victory. “It’s just what Tristan does,” OCS junior D’Siah Bradshaw said. “All the hard work he puts into the summer, all the work he puts into the weight room on the field, those extra hours at practice, that's just hard work. It's not really surprising to me. I know what he’s capable of as a player and as a human being. He’s earned it, for sure.” LHSAA football: 4 storylines to watch for Week 8 in the Monroe area Added senior Jude Turner, “Tristan, that dude is an athlete. He’s blessed by God, and he’s got all kinds of talent. He makes us really, really good.” The Class 1A No. 1 Eagles gave up some chunk plays against the Warriors, including a long kickoff return in the third quarter by St. Fred’s senior JP Guerriero that set up the team’s only touchdown. One of Raymond’s passes was nearly picked off by a Warriors defender but caught by Eagles senior Hunter Oglesbee. There was tension between the two schools located 5 miles away from each other along Highway 165. "It's just a battle every year, and we knew it would be a night," OCS coach Steven Fitzhugh said. "(The Warriors have) come a long way since ( Bayou Jamb ), and they execute their scheme well running the option. (St. Fred's coach Tony) Osborne's done a good job with them, and (senior quarterback Michael) Malloy does a great job leading that entire offense. "They made plays on us (Thursday). Our defense, they bent, but they didn't break. Proud of the way our offense and defense executed and made plays and glad that our kids battled." Both Bradshaw and Turner had touchdown receptions for OCS against St. Fred's (2-5); Raymond hooked up with senior Luke Edwards twice in the endzone. Raymond now has 17 total touchdowns over his last three games. In addition to his four total touchdowns last week against Lincoln Prep , Raymond threw five touchdown passes on Oct. 9 against Bunkie. He said it's a "huge blessing" leading one of north Louisiana's top offenses. "(OCS offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach) Drew Vidrine does a great job with the schemes and the plays," Raymond said. "We've got great weapons around me, a great offensive line, so it's just the perfect recipe for success." Not only did Bradshaw have a touchdown reception against St. Fred's, but he also added two sacks in one drive in the fourth quarter. The Warriors were stopped on fourth down as Bradshaw notched his second sack of the evening. "I didn't think I was going to be able to get one because they ran the ball a lot this game," Bradshaw said. "St. Fred's has a great offense, a very scheme-heavy offense. I was just waiting for my time, and when it showed up, I took the opportunity, and I made it happen." OCS will continue to work toward its ultimate goal of winning its first LHSAA championship since 2022. The Eagles continue district play against General Trass at Steven Fitzhugh Field before heading to Delhi for the regular-season finale. "Winning is winning. You want to be thankful, but you don't want to take it for granted," Raymond said. "We're happy that we got here, but we don't want to stop. We've got to keep going." The Eagles community packed Chip Luffey Field's visitor stands and made their presence felt long before kickoff. They would love to see their team end up at the Caesars Superdome in New Orleans for the fourth time in six seasons. "That's one thing we've always been good at is bringing a crew and having support no matter where we go," Turner said. "It means a lot to the team to have a crowd hollering for you whenever you do something good." This article originally appeared on Monroe News-Star: OCS football defeats St. Fred's behind Tristan Raymond's strong outing

item.title: Why the Falcons need to prioritize Kyle Pitts to solve passing game woes
item.description: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 11: Atlanta tight end Kyle Pitts (8) reacts after catching a touchdown pass during the NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons on October 11th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With less than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Kyle Pitts caught his second pass on a quick out as the Falcons trailed 31-7. It’s normally a standard route and play for a tight end to make in a lopsided matchup. It became the spark the Falcons needed for an unexpected comeback attempt. It also could prove to be the platform to help combat one of the most pressing issues surrounding the Falcons. The Bears soundly outplayed them in every phase of the game, making it an uncompetitive matchup at one point in the second half. The defensive front got bulldozed out of gaps and struggled to maintain its rush integrity against Caleb Williams. The special teams were an absolute disaster, headlined by Zachariah Branch’s nightmare performance that every rookie dreads. Despite those glaring shortcomings and breakdowns, the most damaging aspect of the loss was how overwhelmed the offense looked against Chicago’s pressure looks. For the second consecutive game, Michael Penix Jr. looked incapable of making the right reads and throwing accurately under pressure for long stretches. The coaching staff’s game plan to combat Dennis Allen’s constant schemed-up pressures should raise plenty of questions. Penix Jr. still could have operated better with quicker processing and better feel for blindside pressure. It took until the fourth quarter for him to find some rhythm against Chicago’s defense when they rushed five or six. That’s when Penix Jr. connected with Jahan Dotson for 32 yards on a stop route, where Dotson made a nice hesitation move that turned a solid completion into an explosive gain. It was a sharp play beating Chicago’s five-man pressure. Dotson’s career inconsistency and overall limitations make you cautious about his ability to create separation on the outside often enough to give Penix Jr. high-percentage looks against blitzes. item.content:encoded: ATLANTA, GA - OCTOBER 11: Atlanta tight end Kyle Pitts (8) reacts after catching a touchdown pass during the NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Atlanta Falcons on October 11th, 2026 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, GA. (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With less than 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, Kyle Pitts caught his second pass on a quick out as the Falcons trailed 31-7. It’s normally a standard route and play for a tight end to make in a lopsided matchup. It became the spark the Falcons needed for an unexpected comeback attempt. It also could prove to be the platform to help combat one of the most pressing issues surrounding the Falcons. The Bears soundly outplayed them in every phase of the game, making it an uncompetitive matchup at one point in the second half. The defensive front got bulldozed out of gaps and struggled to maintain its rush integrity against Caleb Williams. The special teams were an absolute disaster, headlined by Zachariah Branch’s nightmare performance that every rookie dreads. Despite those glaring shortcomings and breakdowns, the most damaging aspect of the loss was how overwhelmed the offense looked against Chicago’s pressure looks. For the second consecutive game, Michael Penix Jr. looked incapable of making the right reads and throwing accurately under pressure for long stretches. The coaching staff’s game plan to combat Dennis Allen’s constant schemed-up pressures should raise plenty of questions. Penix Jr. still could have operated better with quicker processing and better feel for blindside pressure. It took until the fourth quarter for him to find some rhythm against Chicago’s defense when they rushed five or six. That’s when Penix Jr. connected with Jahan Dotson for 32 yards on a stop route, where Dotson made a nice hesitation move that turned a solid completion into an explosive gain. It was a sharp play beating Chicago’s five-man pressure. Dotson’s career inconsistency and overall limitations make you cautious about his ability to create separation on the outside often enough to give Penix Jr. high-percentage looks against blitzes. What Pitts did on the next play can be replicated, albeit hopefully not as dramatically for the sake of the Falcons. Dangerous in the slot Per Pro Football Focus, Pitts ran 17 routes from the slot versus Chicago. That was a season high, easily surpassing the seven he ran against Carolina. Some of the high usage from the slot can be attributed to the game script. It was the first game this season where the Falcons were behind all game long with Penix Jr. under center. That proved to be a recipe for success after three quarters of a mostly inept dropback passing game. Chicago brought six with former Falcon Clark Phillips rushing in unblocked. Penix Jr. had to get the ball out quickly again to Pitts outside the numbers. The throw was inside of Pitts, allowing Elijah Hicks to close in for a potential interception. Somehow, the 2025 second-team All-Pro tight end ripped the ball away and juked past Nick McCloud to produce a remarkable 29-yard gain. In the process, he prevented a certain turnover with his improved contested-catch ability. Those types of completions could be an instant solution to the Falcons’ problems against crowded fronts and blitzes. Whether defenses only rush four or bring the entire house with seven or somewhere in between, Baltimore and Chicago have provided a blueprint to rattle Penix Jr. by crowding the line of scrimmage with bodies. Combine that with Kevin Stefanski and Tommy Rees falling short of answers schematically, and you get a dropback passing game that severely limits the offense. That can’t happen against top-tier teams like the Ravens and Bears. Three plays after the highlight-reel reception, Pitts was in the slot again on third down. Chicago rushed six, with Allen being relentless in trying to force Penix Jr. into another off-target throw or sack. Instead, the young quarterback found Pitts uncovered, as Hicks couldn’t make up the ground to stop him. It was a routine touchdown, but it showed how Pitts can be a dependable solution to a glaring problem. Despite being such a unique talent as a deep threat, Pitts can be maximized in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. He proved last year that he can consistently make defenders miss and run through contact after the catch. His blocking has improved enough that he can play more in-line and create more mismatches with his explosiveness off the line of scrimmage. While he should be used more in the slot following Olamide Zaccheaus’ poor play and Branch’s disastrous game, Pitts can also line up more traditionally as a tight end to bolster the Falcons’ aerial attack. Being quick and decisive After Jessie Bates connected on his signature peanut punch to force a fumble, as he does multiple times a year, it didn’t take long for Penix Jr. to go back to Pitts. Operating in no-huddle, they slowed Chicago’s pressure plan and capitalized on Pitts being isolated inside with an undersized defensive back. Targeting that mismatch helped Penix Jr. find Pitts to convert on third and nine. They connected again on the next play to get in the end zone, putting the Falcons within striking distance of an outrageous comeback. A slight rub by Zaccheaus on the slant-flat concept gave Pitts the space necessary to score his second touchdown of the game. As much as fans want to see Pitts be utilized like the unicorn he was projected to be, the coaching staff needs him more than ever as a possession pass-catcher in these situations to give Penix Jr. an immediate option under pressure. There will be instances where he can thrive in the slot, like against Chicago. He could also line up as an in-line tight end, chipping an edge rusher and serving as a reliable outlet underneath. Whatever the play design, Pitts needs to be a bigger focal point to make the passing game more efficient. According to TruMedia, the Bears blitzed Penix Jr. on an alarming 48.7 percent of his dropbacks. That could increase in upcoming matchups against Todd Bowles, Steve Spagnuolo, and Brian Flores. Those coaches won’t hesitate to ramp up the pressure on any quarterback, let alone a young passer who isn’t reacting well when seven defenders are lined up across the line of scrimmage. The coaching staff will have to do its share schematically to solidify their protection plan. Making Pitts a bigger focal point in the passing game is the other vital step to punish defenses for constantly blitzing. Signs are emerging in recent weeks, as Pitts’ target share has increased over the last three games. That said, those targets have to come earlier in games. Pitts catching only his second pass late in what was arguably the Falcons’ most disappointing performance of the season (with a starting-caliber quarterback under center) indicates he needs to be prioritized far more early and often.

item.title: Dybala’s likely return date revealed after latest medical tests
item.description: Dybala’s likely return date revealed after latest medical tests Paulo Dybala is expected to miss Saturday’s Serie A match against Napoli, but Roma hope the Argentine will be available for the following mid-week fixture against Cagliari. Roma star Dybala is close to returning to action. According to Sky Sport Italia , the latest medical tests showed that the Argentine’s recovery is progressing well. ISTANBUL, TURKEY – SEPTEMBER 10: Paulo Dybala of AS Roma gestures during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Fenerbahce SK and AS Roma at Fenerbahce Sükrü Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi on September 10, 2026 in Istanbul, Turkey. (Photo by Burak Kara/Getty Images) Although Dybala is expected to miss tomorrow’s big Serie A match against Napoli at the Stadio Maradona, Roma are confident their star attacker will be in the squad for next Tuesday’s home league game against Cagliari. Dybala has missed the last two games against Genoa in Serie A and Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League due to a calf injury. DORTMUND, GERMANY – AUGUST 15: Paulo Dybala of AS Roma runs with the ball during the pre-season friendly match between Borussia Dortmund and AS Roma at Signal Iduna Park on August 15, 2026 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Christof Koepsel/Getty Images) ROME, ITALY – AUGUST 24: Donyell Malen with Paulo Dybala and Wesley Franca of AS Roma celebrates during the Serie A match between AS Roma and ACF Fiorentina at Stadio Olimpico on August 24, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) He has provided four assists in eight appearances across all competitions this season. Roma sit third in the Serie A table with 17 points, two fewer than table leaders Lazio and Inter. The Giallorossi have scored 16 goals in seven league games and conceded only three, giving them the league’s best defence.

item.title: Former NFL player shares why he thinks Kenneth Walker ‘regression’ is going to start this week
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Kenneth Walker has been in superb form during the first six weeks of the season, but Leger Douzable has suggested he is due for a regression, which could start this week. Walker joined the Kansas City Chiefs earlier in 2026 after helping the Seattle Seahawks secure the Super Bowl. He now leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with his team 5-0 going into their Week 7 tie against the Seahawks. But Douzable has suggested that Walker’s ‘regression’ will start this week because Seattle have a defence which is ‘tough’ to run the football against. Speaking via NFL on CBS, he said: “[Kenneth Walker] is due for a regression, which you would assume is going to happen because he’s played at, at this pace, it’s ridiculous, and I think it starts this week just because that is a tough defence to run the football against.” He added: “You don’t think that Macdonald is going to know that the key focal point of the Kansas City offence is to minimise what Kenneth Walker III does. He’s going to do everything in his power to make sure that Mahomes and that Chiefs offence is in second and third and long. That way their pass rushers can really get after the quarterback.” It remains to be seen if the Seahawks, who are 3-3 going into this game, have the ability to stop both Walker and Patrick Mahomes to put an end to the Chiefs’ winning streak. item.title: ‘We’ll look for a way out’: Man Utd star’s agent makes frank admission over his player’s game time
item.description: ‘We’ll look for a way out’: Man Utd star’s agent makes frank admission over his player’s game time Diego Leon’s agent has revealed that they will be exploring a move elsewhere if the player is not granted any first-team minutes between now and the end of 2026. The 19-year-old has yet to make his Manchester United debut since signing from Cerro Porteno in a deal worth up to £7 million. Diego Leon: The state of play Leon has been featuring prominently with the Under-21s, but is seemingly chomping at the bit to be called up to the senior squad and stake his claim. The fact that United are facing a crisis in his position at left-back has likely prompted his agent to go public with the youngster’s desire to feature under Michael Carrick, as it would provide one more option in Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu’s absences. However, fellow academy star and left-back Harry Amass was kept at Old Trafford over the summer for depth, but Noussair Mazraoui and even Diogo Dalot have been preferred in the role in recent weeks, showing Carrick is opting for experience. What Leon’s agent had to say “If there isn’t a plan to break into the first team between December and January, we’ll look for a way out for him. A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester,” said Leon’s representative, Renato Bittar (via Sport Witness ). “The Championship is an option, as are other European leagues, but we don’t want to leave here. He’s performing well with the U21 team, he’s training well, and his physical condition is excellent.” There may be more options for Leon to earn some minutes when United kick off their FA Cup campaign in the coming months, though their premature Carabao Cup exit may have convinced Carrick to go full-strength in order to avoid another embarrassment. item.title: Steelers Get Good News on Alex Highsmith
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith in a game against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith (groin) is good to go for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Highsmith does not have an injury designation after dealing with a groin issue, which limited him during the team’s practices at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex on Wednesday and Thursday. Highsmith was an estimated full practice participant on Friday. The Steelers cancelled Friday’s practice in Paris due to rain and wind in the forecast. With three sacks, Highsmith currently ranks second on the team, behind only fellow outside linebacker T.J. Watt (4.5). Nick Herbig has posted two and cornerback Jalen Ramsey just as many, both coming in an overtime win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Sunday. Highsmith also has 11 combined tackles and a pass defended on the season. Pittsburgh Steelers outside linebacker Alex Highsmith after the Steelers’ 272-22 win voer the Baltimore Ravens’ on Dec. 7, 2025. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Some speculated after the Steelers extended Herbig’s contract in the offseason that Highsmith might have been on the trade block. Highsmith talked during training camp about his future in Pittsburgh. “I want to be a Steeler for life,” Highsmith said. “I just want to go out there and do whatever I can to help bring another Super Bowl to this team, another Super Bowl to this city. I do want to be a Steeler for life. Just excited for this year, and obviously, our group. We’re the best group in the league edge-wise. The three of us and Jack (Sawyer). Just really, really excited for the group that we have. I think there’s going to be some special things.” Brendan Howe contributed. Watt’s Injury Status Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: LeBron James Reacts to Donald Trump Blasting Him Over National Anthem
item.description: LeBron James and Donald Trump - LeBron James and Donald Trump (Sarah Stier and Eric Lee/Getty Images) LeBron James finally broke his silence regarding criticism from President Donald Trump , who called out his behavior during the national anthem ahead of the Philadelphia 76ers and New York Knicks game at Madison Square Garden earlier in the week. Speaking to reporters on Thursday night during a press conferenc e after the game, which saw the 76ers beat the Cleveland Cavaliers in a 114-106 comeback victory, James brushed off the controversy with a brief response: “It’s a slow news day at the office, you know. Slow news day in the office.” LeBron James responds to Donald Trump taking shots at him with a BRUTAL one liner: “Slow news day at the office, you know.” https://t.co/Y4Qa0lHD6a — Deuce World (@deuceworldx) October 23, 2026 The tension began after Trump shared a video on Truth Social just hours before, which showed James practicing a golf swing and a jump shot while the anthem played, while his 76ers teammates mostly stood still. In the post, Trump slammed the four-time NBA champion as a “TOTAL DISGRACE” and demanded an apology for American veterans and heroes who died for the flag. Trump: “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP” — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 22, 2026 Trump’s remarks add another chapter to a long-running public feud between the two, which spans over a decade of political clashes, critical social media jabs, and James’ long history of activism on racial equality and social justice issues. It dates back to 2017 when James called Trump a “bum” on social media after the White House rescinded an invitation to Stephen Curry and the Golden State Warriors, stating that visiting the nation’s capital was a great honor “until you showed up.” On social media, users have responded to the most recent rift between James and Trump. One user commented under one of the posts: “Hilarious thing to say to possibly the most famous athlete in America right before the midterms. Trump is in a class of his own.” Another user wrote : “that one liner was actually too smooth, he really just dismissed him like that.” This isn’t the first time that athletes have had issues with Trump and his administration. Earlier this year, former Philadelphia Eagles safety Brian Dawkins and the NFL pushed back against the Department of Homeland Security after the agency used unauthorized footage of the retired athlete in a post about immigration and enforcement efforts. Related NFL and Eagles' Brian Dawkins Demand Trump Admin Take Down Video 76ers head coach Nick Nurse addressed the media before Thursday night’s game, but chose instead to focus on basketball. item.title: Michael Carrick addresses Bruno Fernandes captaincy after Man United outburst in Como
item.description: Michael Carrick maintains he will “do what is best for this football club” after being pushed over Bruno Fernandes ’ future as Manchester United captain. The Portuguese’s astonishing outburst in Como following a humiliating Champions League defeat, questioning Carrick’s strategy and the team’s decision to press against the Italians. Speculation has followed over whether Fernandes will face internal discipline, just a week after Lisandro Martinez’s criticism of the club. But Carrick remains defiant and urged his group to show resiliency , though he stopped short of confirming his decision over Fernandes for this weekend’s Premier League clash with Bournemouth, instead sharing a mysterious stance over his latest problem. “The most important thing is the team and the dynamics of the squad and the football club and I always do what is best for the club,” Carrick noted. “Whatever the situation is I will do what is best for the football club. (Getty) ”If I have spoken to him or I haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail.” Carrick then reiterated how the club must revert back to its values and show how resilient they can be after a torrid run of form. “It's important to recognise we haven't been doing it,” Carrick added. “The foundation of the football club, the values of the football club have been put down for many years. I understand and get every one of them. It's humility, hard work and being proud to live up to the values. “There's a resilience about this club that's been there for a long time. It runs very deep, I've seen it with my own eyes, I've felt it. “We can never lose that, it inspires me a lot to live up to that. We’ve shown it, for a good period of time, we’re capable of it, it’s a moment where it’s not gone well. Respect what it takes to win. I’m not entitled to be here, that cannot be at this football club, it doesn’t mean you’re entitled to win. It takes hard work and sacrifice.” United are seven games without a win in all competitions and sit 13th in the Premier League with the Cherries visiting Old Trafford on Sunday following a 4-4 draw in the same fixture last season.

item.title: Cleveland Browns News and Rumors 10/23/26: Scouting the Trap
item.description: theOBR CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans! THE DAILY BLOVIATION Two weeks ago, the Browns came off a walk-off win over the Steelers, flew to New Jersey to play a one-win team in the rain, and lost 17-12. Fred Greetham's piece this morning is titled " Browns Must Learn the Lesson of the Jets Loss ." Chris Easterling calls the Titans " the ultimate trap opponent ." Jared Verse, for his part, doesn't believe in trap games. "Every team has a 'Dawg,'" he said. My paranoia about all things, but particularly positive expectations about the Browns, has been well documented. Pick any random edition of this Massive Morning Missive, and you’re sure to find something that will make you nod to yourself and say out loud, “Yep, he’s paranoid.” Also, “How much coffee does this guy drink ?” 27 years of this, my friends. 27 years. And the answer is “a lot.” So, it makes sense that I believe in trap games. I've watched this franchise step in more than a few. I'd also point out that the last time these teams met, last Dec. 7 in Cleveland, the Titans jumped out 14-3 in the first quarter, Tony Pollard ran for a career-high 161 yards, and Tennessee won 31-29 . So before anybody pencils in 5-2, let's take a walk through Nashville. THE INFIRMARY: This time of year, injury reports might be the best clue as to how a team is trending. The Titans are healthier than we are, which isn't saying much, because almost everybody is. Their Thursday injury report has seven names. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing Thursday. Pollard sat Thursday and Tyjae Spears sat Wednesday, both listed as rest. Safeties Kevin Winston Jr. (quad), who has missed the last two games, and Tony Adams (ankle) were limited both days. Linebacker Dorian Mausi is practicing fully on his way back from injured reserve. Ridley is also on the trade block, per Titans On SI , at a "career-low 13.5 receiving yards per game." So, factor that in accordingly. Our list is longer. Quincy Williams missed Thursday with a neck injury, and Mike Rutenberg wouldn't say whether he'll play. Of all the weeks for that to happen, it's the one where Quincy faces Robert Saleh, his old head coach with the Jets. Carson Schwesinger, Grant Delpit and Elgton Jenkins came back as limited participants, per PFT , and Mason Graham is expected back . Friday's reports, with game statuses, come out this afternoon. THE JORDAN ELLIOTT SITUATION: On Oct. 15, after an argument with left tackle JC Latham at practice, Elliott was sent off the field and went to his car in the players' lot to get his gun. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers talked him down. A source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo the gun never left the parking spot. The Titans released Elliott on Tuesday, and Saleh confirmed the details Wednesday, calling it "a call for help more than a criminal act," per ESPN . The Titans notified the league, which is reviewing it, per the Tennessean . On the field, the Titans lose
item.content:encoded: theOBR CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans! THE DAILY BLOVIATION Two weeks ago, the Browns came off a walk-off win over the Steelers, flew to New Jersey to play a one-win team in the rain, and lost 17-12. Fred Greetham's piece this morning is titled " Browns Must Learn the Lesson of the Jets Loss ." Chris Easterling calls the Titans " the ultimate trap opponent ." Jared Verse, for his part, doesn't believe in trap games. "Every team has a 'Dawg,'" he said. My paranoia about all things, but particularly positive expectations about the Browns, has been well documented. Pick any random edition of this Massive Morning Missive, and you’re sure to find something that will make you nod to yourself and say out loud, “Yep, he’s paranoid.” Also, “How much coffee does this guy drink ?” 27 years of this, my friends. 27 years. And the answer is “a lot.” So, it makes sense that I believe in trap games. I've watched this franchise step in more than a few. I'd also point out that the last time these teams met, last Dec. 7 in Cleveland, the Titans jumped out 14-3 in the first quarter, Tony Pollard ran for a career-high 161 yards, and Tennessee won 31-29 . So before anybody pencils in 5-2, let's take a walk through Nashville. THE INFIRMARY: This time of year, injury reports might be the best clue as to how a team is trending. The Titans are healthier than we are, which isn't saying much, because almost everybody is. Their Thursday injury report has seven names. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing Thursday. Pollard sat Thursday and Tyjae Spears sat Wednesday, both listed as rest. Safeties Kevin Winston Jr. (quad), who has missed the last two games, and Tony Adams (ankle) were limited both days. Linebacker Dorian Mausi is practicing fully on his way back from injured reserve. Ridley is also on the trade block, per Titans On SI , at a "career-low 13.5 receiving yards per game." So, factor that in accordingly. Our list is longer. Quincy Williams missed Thursday with a neck injury, and Mike Rutenberg wouldn't say whether he'll play. Of all the weeks for that to happen, it's the one where Quincy faces Robert Saleh, his old head coach with the Jets. Carson Schwesinger, Grant Delpit and Elgton Jenkins came back as limited participants, per PFT , and Mason Graham is expected back . Friday's reports, with game statuses, come out this afternoon. THE JORDAN ELLIOTT SITUATION: On Oct. 15, after an argument with left tackle JC Latham at practice, Elliott was sent off the field and went to his car in the players' lot to get his gun. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers talked him down. A source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo the gun never left the parking spot. The Titans released Elliott on Tuesday, and Saleh confirmed the details Wednesday, calling it "a call for help more than a criminal act," per ESPN . The Titans notified the league, which is reviewing it, per the Tennessean . On the field, the Titans lose a run-stopping tackle who followed Saleh from San Francisco, though he'd already been inactive for the Colts game. In Ask the Insiders, Tdfcpny is asking whether Elliott will ever play again . I don't know. He spent four years here after the Browns drafted him in the third round in 2020, and the football is the least important part of this one. I hope he gets the help he obviously needs. THE TITANS OFFENSE: It's bad. The Titans are last in the league in total offense at 236.3 yards a game and tied for 31st in scoring at 14.0, per their own site . They're 32nd in time of possession at 24 minutes a game , 26th on third down and 29th in red zone touchdown rate, per Pro Football Reference . They beat the Colts while getting outgained 399-186 . Two tendencies jump out. First, timing. Easterling found the Titans have played opponents even, 20-20, in the first quarter, then been outscored 62-3 in the second. The Browns have been outscored 44-6 in the first quarter, and the second is our best. The first quarter on Sunday could be interesting. Prepare to grimace, but know better times soon follow. Second, the ball comes out fast and short. Cam Ward was sacked 55 times last year, tied for the league lead . This year the line has allowed only 10 sacks, but Ward has just 10 completions of 20-plus yards and one of 40-plus, per Titans On SI , which blames offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's "milquetoast scheme" about as much as the quarterback. Our defense has 19 sacks, second in the league. Something has to give there too. CAM WARD: The first overall pick in 2025 is 4-19 as a starter, and AP notes he narrowly avoided becoming only the second quarterback of the common draft era to lose 20 of his first 23 starts. Per Pro Football Reference, the first was likely the world-famous Steve DeBerg. Ward has 998 yards, four touchdowns, four interceptions and a 39.5 QBR, 29th in the league. Against the Colts he went 11-for-22 for 102 yards, his lowest total in any game he's finished. Saleh: "It's not all on the quarterback... But he is the face of the offense and he's got to play at a higher level." Ward: "We still know we are behind the eight-ball." Todd Monken was kinder Wednesday. He said everyone tells him Ward is "there early, super diligent, highly competitive. That's a great starting point for a franchise quarterback." Cleveland is the last city on earth that should snicker at a young quarterback's rough second season. But I'd like our pass rush to make it rougher for one more Sunday. CARNELL TATE: This is the Titan I've watched most, because he was a Buckeye. The fourth overall pick leads Tennessee with 29 catches for 344 yards in five games, and he caught his first NFL touchdown against the Colts, part of a six-catch, 70-yard day. Saleh is gushing : "He looked juicy right there... He just looked like a top five pick." Monken, who first met Tate when he visited Georgia as a recruit, said Wednesday that "he's wired like the guys we drafted." If I'm Rutenberg, Denzel Ward spends Sunday afternoon wherever Tate is. THE DEFENSE: This is the realm of the Titans that can actually beat us, especially given the situation with the Browns' anemic running game. Saleh brought his attack-style front four, and Monken says they're "a lot like us." The centerpiece is Jeffery Simmons, the defensive tackle Ben Solak picked for Defensive Player of the Year through six weeks. He has four sacks and six tackles for loss , and he moves around the interior, so both our guards will see him, including rookie Austin Barber in his seventh NFL start. Tytus Howard faced Simmons nine times with Houston, and his advice was simple: "He has no weaknesses in his game... You have to bring it to him and don't back down... you just have to stand ten toes." Against the Colts, Tennessee had six sacks and three takeaways. Simmons had two sacks and forced and recovered a fumble, and Jermaine Johnson II added two more sacks. This defense allows about 21.5 points a game, which isn't the reason the Titans are 1-5. The Browns’ line has allowed a league-high 24 sacks. Not crazy about this matchup. If that offensive line is going to gel, now would be a really good time. THE THIRD PHASE: John Fassel's special teams won the Colts game with a blocked punt returned for the go-ahead touchdown, a 58-yard Chimere Dike punt return and four Joey Slye field goals, including a 56-yarder. The Jets game turned on a special teams mistake too. Please hang on to the ball. So that's the Titans. They can't move the ball, they play defense like they mean it, they block punts, and their best young player is a Buckeye getting better every week. That's the exact profile of a team that beats you 13-10 in a game you were supposed to win. They've also lost four straight at home, and they're desperate. Verse is right that it isn't a trap game. It's just a game, and the Browns have to show up for the first quarter of it this time around. A good sign would be if they could pre

item.title: Carrick vows he will turn Man Utd form around and defends his players
item.description: Carrick vows he will turn Man Utd form around and defends his players Michael Carrick has dismissed suggestions of a divided Manchester United dressing room and insisted his side are capable of turning their fortunes around. United have endured another difficult spell, but Carrick remains adamant there is unity within the squad. “It’s not divided, no,” the United boss said. “We just need to get back to what we’re doing best and we will.” Stay up to date with all the latest Manchester United news by joining our Man Utd WhatsApp channel . Carrick was also asked about Bruno Fernandes but refused to reveal whether he has held talks with the United captain after comments he made questioning the team’s tactics in the defeat to Como. “If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said. Despite admitting recent results have hurt, Carrick says he is using that frustration as motivation to change United’s direction. “It hurts an awful lot but it doesn’t stop me,” he said. “That hurt is used as pure motivation and inspiration to want more, to expect more, to work for more, and to get us going in that different direction. “It feels at times like it can be a long way away but it doesn’t take too much to flip the other way and we’re more than capable of doing that. “I totally believe that. And we will win football matches.” If you enjoy our articles, help us out by making Hayters.com one of your preferred sources on Google by clicking here.

item.title: CHN Daily: Blackhawks Return; Suzuki Injured; NHL Trade Board
item.description: For the first time in nearly one week, it’s Game Day for the Chicago Blackhawks! After five days off from game action, the Blackhawks continue their homestand with an original-six matchup against the Montreal Canadiens on Friday night. Since their last outing on Saturday, the Blackhawks held three practices this week to prepare for the Canadiens. However, Bowen Byram didn’t participate in any of the sessions while still recovering from an upper-body injury. Byram’s status for Friday’s game remains cloudy, but head coach Jeff Blashill provided a somewhat positive update after yesterday’s practice. More in the links for the Blackhawks latest injury news. Around the league, an updated NHL trade board, the latest rumors surrounding Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings, and injury news on the Montreal Canadiens’ captain. All that & more in the Daily! Blackhawks Game Recaps, News & Trade Rumors While Bowen Byram wasn’t on the ice with his teammates during practice this week, Andrew Mangiapane returned from the lower-body injury he suffered on opening night. Mangiapane shed the non-contact sweater for the first time at Thursday’s practice, although he didn’t participate in line rushes. item.content:encoded: For the first time in nearly one week, it’s Game Day for the Chicago Blackhawks! After five days off from game action, the Blackhawks continue their homestand with an original-six matchup against the Montreal Canadiens on Friday night. Since their last outing on Saturday, the Blackhawks held three practices this week to prepare for the Canadiens. However, Bowen Byram didn’t participate in any of the sessions while still recovering from an upper-body injury. Byram’s status for Friday’s game remains cloudy, but head coach Jeff Blashill provided a somewhat positive update after yesterday’s practice. More in the links for the Blackhawks latest injury news. Around the league, an updated NHL trade board, the latest rumors surrounding Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings, and injury news on the Montreal Canadiens’ captain. All that & more in the Daily! Nick Kypreos listed his Trade Board 2.0 , with potential fits for Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck as the main topics. Hellebuyck returns from his suspension today, while Larkin has expanded his trade list. Do we get any trades this weekend? Pittsburgh Hockey Now: The Pittsburgh Penguins have placed forwards Bryan Rust and Ben Kindel on injured reserve. Rust got hurt Monday in a loss at Utah. Kindel had a vasovagal episode on the team plane Tuesday. Montreal Hockey Now: Reigning Selke Trophy winner and Montreal Canadiens captain Nick Suzuki won’t be in the lineup against the Blackhawks on Friday, as he’s been ruled out for 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. Marc Dumont writes that the Habs face their ultimate stress test without Suzuki. Boston Hockey Now: The Boston Bruins rolled past the Nashville Predators 6-0 on Thursday, extending their current point streak to seven games. David Pastrnak tallied four points (2G, 2A), while Michael DiPietro recorded his first career NHL shutout. TSN: Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl each tallied five points (2G, 3A) in the Edmonton Oilers’ 6-5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday. McDavid became the second player in NHL history to record three five-point outings in the first 10 games of a season, joining Hall of Famer Mario Lemieux. CBC: Roope Hintz tallied the game-tying goal with two minutes remaining in regulation, then scored the overtime winner to lift the Dallas Stars to a come-from-behind 3-2 win over the Winnipeg Jets. APNews: Justin Barron’s first career four-point game led the St. Louis Blues to a dominant 6-2 victory over the Vegas Golden Knights on Thursday. Dylan Holloway (2G, 1A) and Jimmy Snuggerud (1G, 1A) also had multi-point performances. The 26-year-old winger will be a restricted free agent at the end of this season. Voronkov has tallied at least 17 goals in each of his first three NHL seasons. item.title: Steelers’ D.K. Metcalf Put on Notice Days Before Saints Matchup
item.description: NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal argued Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf is no longer the team's top wideout entering Week 7. Getty NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal argued Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf is no longer the team's top wideout entering Week 7. Getty Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard is off to a strong start in his rookie career. Getty Veteran wide receiver D.K. Metcalf turned in one of his better games of the young 2026 season in the Pittsburgh Steelers comeback victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Metcalf hauled in a season-high 11 catches for 93 yards. The Steelers needed every bit of that production. The team required overtime to defeat the 1-5 Buccaneers 26-19. In the victory, Metcalf was one of only two wideouts to catch a pass. The big game is something for Metcalf to build on going forward. But NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal isn’t sure the veteran is still the top option in the Steelers passing game. This week, Rosenthal argued that is now Pittsburgh’s sensational rookie Germie Bernard. who also had 11 catches against the Buccaneers. “Watch Germie Bernard for the Steelers,” Rosenthal said on his NFL Daily podcast , via Steelers Now’s Aaron Becker . “A rookie that Aaron Rodgers absolutely trusts and can do a little bit of everything really well. When I saw the deceleration and his ability to go from full speed to stopping in a second, it reminded me of Chris Olave . Not saying he’s going to be Chris Olave. He doesn’t have that juice, but a little more juice than expected. I look at him as the 1A, and DK Metcalf right now, coming off his best game of the year, as the 1B.” Bernard caught the game-winning touchdown in overtime against the Buccaneers. The rookie has reached at least 80 receiving yards in each of the past two contests. Metcalf had 93 receiving yards on his 11 receptions Sunday. Is Steelers’ D.K. Metcalf Giving Way to Rookie Germie Bernard? Getty NFL analyst Gregg Rosenthal argued Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver D.K. Metcalf is no longer the team’s top wideout entering Week 7. Metcalf hasn’t been very consistent this season. Particularly early in the year, he dealt with drops. The veteran broke out of his funk with five catches and 115 yards versus the Cleveland Browns in Week 4. But he then followed that up with just three receptions for 12 yards in Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts . Still, it’s a little hard to believe a pundit would suggest Metcalf isn’t still quarterback Aaron Rodgers’s favorite target. Even with Bernard coming on the past couple weeks, Metcalf has received 20 more targets than the rookie this season. Metcalf also leads the Steelers with 30 catches and 318 receiving yards. Only running back Jaylen Warren has more yards from scrimmage for the team. item.title: Carrick defends himself: It was unacceptable, but we'll bounce back
item.description: Carrick defends himself: It was unacceptable, but we'll bounce back Michael Carrick has said Manchester United must end "a run we're not happy with at all". Manchester United are winless in seven games across all competitions and suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League in midweek. Tensions have come to light following recent comments from players, including Lisandro Martínez and Bruno Fernandes, who have strongly criticised the club's hierarchy. Fernandes questioned Carrick's tactics during the defeat in Como, with the manager under pressure ahead of this weekend's match against Bournemouth. Carrick declined to comment on whether he had spoken to Fernandes about his remarks this week, or whether he had considered stripping the 32-year-old of the captaincy. At his pre-match press conference , Carrick said the Red Devils must bounce back from an "unacceptable" performance in the Champions League. Manchester United manager Carrick demands a response after Como thrashing: "We've had a run we're not happy with at all". "I just want to say a few things, really. We haven't had a good time lately. I think that's pretty obvious. So I fully accept what we're going through at the moment." "We had five months of relative success, a period when I was happy with a lot of what I was seeing and what we were doing as a team." "Recently we haven't been good enough. We've had a run we're not happy with at all." "Wednesday was a bad night. It was a bad night for many reasons. It hurt me a lot." "Obviously it hurt to see how we played, to see how the game unfolded. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable." "The fans are a fundamental part of this football club. For them to put in the effort, the time and the money they invest, only to feel what we all felt on Wednesday—it was a very tough moment." item.title: Jalen Hurts’ injury could be a blessing in disguise for the Eagles
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Jalen Hurts’ health is the only thing that matters right now. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and the team expects him to make a full recovery. Still, his absence also leaves Philadelphia facing an uncomfortable reality: This season could be the opportunity the franchise needs to make a change at head coach. The Eagles are 2-4, riding a four-game losing streak, and their offense has looked completely lost for stretches of the young season. The defense has its own problems, but the recurring offensive dysfunction is becoming impossible to ignore. Nick Sirianni has delivered tremendous highs in Philadelphia, including a Super Bowl championship. However, the Eagles have repeatedly struggled to establish a consistent offensive identity. If Hurts’ absence exposes those issues even further, ownership should use the offseason to move in a different direction. The Offensive Coordinator Carousel Is Unsustainable Sirianni’s biggest problem might be the structure he has created around himself. Philadelphia has cycled through offensive coordinators at an alarming rate. Shane Steichen left after the 2022 season to become the Indianapolis Colts’ head coach. Brian Johnson followed, then Kellen Moore arrived and helped the Eagles win the Super Bowl before leaving to become the New Orleans Saints’ head coach. Now Sean Mannion is tasked with getting the offense back on track. Every new coordinator brings a different philosophy, terminology, and approach. Quarterbacks and receivers must adjust, the offensive line must learn new concepts, and the entire unit needs time to build chemistry. That instability is especially damaging in an NFL increasingly defined by offensive innovation and continuity. Sirianni’s supporters can point to the Super Bowl trophy and argue that his approach works. That’s fair, but a successful head coach should build a structure that survives staff turnover, rather than repeatedly starting over whenever an assistant gets a better opportunity. Sirianni also occupies an awkward middle ground. He delegates play-calling but remains heavily involved in shaping the offense. If the offense struggles, it’s difficult to determine where the coordinator’s responsibility ends, and the head coach’s begins. Philadelphia needs a clear offensive identity and a head coach who can establish it. This Is an Opportunity to Start Fresh The Eagles shouldn’t blow up their roster. item.content:encoded: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Jalen Hurts’ health is the only thing that matters right now. The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, and the team expects him to make a full recovery. Still, his absence also leaves Philadelphia facing an uncomfortable reality: This season could be the opportunity the franchise needs to make a change at head coach. The Eagles are 2-4, riding a four-game losing streak, and their offense has looked completely lost for stretches of the young season. The defense has its own problems, but the recurring offensive dysfunction is becoming impossible to ignore. Nick Sirianni has delivered tremendous highs in Philadelphia, including a Super Bowl championship. However, the Eagles have repeatedly struggled to establish a consistent offensive identity. If Hurts’ absence exposes those issues even further, ownership should use the offseason to move in a different direction. The Offensive Coordinator Carousel Is Unsustainable Sirianni’s biggest problem might be the structure he has created around himself. Philadelphia has cycled through offensive coordinators at an alarming rate. Shane Steichen left after the 2022 season to become the Indianapolis Colts’ head coach. Brian Johnson followed, then Kellen Moore arrived and helped the Eagles win the Super Bowl before leaving to become the New Orleans Saints’ head coach. Now Sean Mannion is tasked with getting the offense back on track. Every new coordinator brings a different philosophy, terminology, and approach. Quarterbacks and receivers must adjust, the offensive line must learn new concepts, and the entire unit needs time to build chemistry. That instability is especially damaging in an NFL increasingly defined by offensive innovation and continuity. Sirianni’s supporters can point to the Super Bowl trophy and argue that his approach works. That’s fair, but a successful head coach should build a structure that survives staff turnover, rather than repeatedly starting over whenever an assistant gets a better opportunity. Sirianni also occupies an awkward middle ground. He delegates play-calling but remains heavily involved in shaping the offense. If the offense struggles, it’s difficult to determine where the coordinator’s responsibility ends, and the head coach’s begins. Philadelphia needs a clear offensive identity and a head coach who can establish it. This Is an Opportunity to Start Fresh The Eagles shouldn’t blow up their roster. They still have the foundation of a championship team. Hurts remains their franchise quarterback. DeVonta Smith is an established playmaker, while Jalen Carter, Cooper DeJean, and Quinyon Mitchell give Philadelphia promising young talent to build around. The problem isn’t a lack of talent. It’s whether the current coaching structure can consistently maximize it. Philadelphia’s recent collapses have been particularly concerning. The offense has struggled to score after halftime, and the losses to Chicago, Jacksonville, and Los Angeles exposed a team that too often looks incapable of adjusting when things go wrong. Injuries have unquestionably played a role. Lane Johnson’s retirement, Cam Jurgens’ departure, injuries to Landon Dickerson and Saquon Barkley, and DeVonta Smith’s absences have made life difficult. Hurts’ diagnosis only adds to the adversity. But injuries don’t explain every schematic problem or every second-half collapse. And if the Eagles finish with a losing record, ownership will have to decide whether the current direction is worth another season. Don’t Let a Respectable Finish Cloud the Decision The biggest danger for Philadelphia is finishing just well enough to avoid making a difficult decision. Tanner McKee could keep the offense competitive. The defense could win games, and the NFC East could provide a path to the playoffs. If the Eagles scrape together a respectable finish, the pressure to retain Sirianni will grow. But a few wins wouldn’t erase the larger issues. Philadelphia needs to evaluate the season honestly, determine whether Sirianni is the right person to lead its next championship push, and make a decision based on the long-term outlook rather than the final win total. If the answer is no, the offseason is the time to move on. A coaching change would give the Eagles an opportunity to hire an offensive-minded head coach with a clear vision, build continuity around Hurts, and use their draft capital to address an aging and increasingly injury-prone roster. The Eagles don’t need to start from scratch. They need to stop repeating the same cycle. Jalen Hurts’ injury is a serious setback, and nobody should pretend otherwise. But if this season finally forces Philadelphia to confront its coaching problem, the organization could emerge better positioned for the future. The championship window isn’t necessarily closed. It might simply be time for someone new to lead it. At the New Balance Arena, Atalanta have the edge in their duels with Frosinone: three wins in four games. Frosinone have never won on Atalanta’s ground, with one draw recorded. item.title: Xabi Alonso rules out defender for Tottenham game, but says another “fine” to play
item.description: Xabi Alonso rules out defender for Tottenham game, but says another “fine” to play Pep Chavarria has been ruled out of tomorrow’s game against Tottenham by Xabi Alonso in today’s press conference. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. The injury situation at Chelsea right now is OK – but it’s heading in the wrong direction. A few players were already out, and we added Reece James, Emi Martinez and Pep Chavarria to that list last week. The squad is deep and it’s not time to panic just yet, but Xabi Alonso had to give an update on a few players today. One full back ruled out, another “fine” Malo Gusto (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) We know that Martinez and James will be out for a while, so what we wanted to know about was the injury we had little information on – the problem that caused Chavarria to pull out of the Everton game at the last minute last week. Alonso didn’t give much information (he never does), but did confirm that the Spaniard won’t be ready for tomorrow’s game against Spurs. “Malo [Gusto] is fine. Pep is training a little bit more but he is not going to make it.” It sounds like he will be back in a week at most, and could even be ready for the game against Liverpool in midweek. Jorrel Hato will continue on the left, with Marco Palestra fit to come on and play on either side if needed. In other news… The change in strategy from Chelsea’s owners has been praised by Gus Poyet. Joao Pedro has been speaking about his relationship with Cole Palmer and how quickly it developed after his arrival. A Chelsea rising star has been compared to Arsenal’s Riccardo Calafiori by pundits.

item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure manager faces her latest test against Spurs It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 in two games are not the side whose manager is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches – but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham City at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Liew
item.content:encoded: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.description: Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead. After defeats by Ferencvaros and Benfica in their first two league phase fixtures, Martin O’Neill’s side struggled to impose themselves on the visitors who were neat and tidy without really testing Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone. Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Niall McVeigh
item.content:encoded: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.description: The reigning champions must deal with the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for some time, while fans at Anfield were thrilled by Rio Ngumoha Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday , but the reigning champions lost the best player in last season’s tournament, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. This autumn has seen much lobbying for the Ballon d’Or, with the Georgian a popular choice, despite his absence from the World Cup. He is expected to be out for six months, although Rodri’s comeback from serious injury – he was rested by Barcelona on Tuesday until coming off the bench in the 60th minute – shows it can take far longer than that for players to rediscover their highest level. item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Philipp Lahm
item.content:encoded: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...
